title: Partille World Cup 2027
content:
On July 5–10 2027 it’s time again for Partille World Cup – The largest international handball event in the world and one of the top-events of all kinds of youth sports! Annually there are 23.000 participants from around 40 countries divided into 1.400 teams.

World of Handball

Partille World Cup is about experiences and encounters with foreign cultures, the Opening Festival is an important statement. The event is international in its nature and diversity is an important part of the event’s soul. Combined with global interests such as song and music, curiosity becomes greater and barriers less. The meeting between players often results in good relationships and not infrequently to lifelong friendships. The opening will take place in Scandinavium, partillecup.com/opening-ceremony

The centres

Heden and Kviberg are our largest field areas in terms of number of pitches and stands. In addition to great international handball you will also find our event areas where fun activities and competitions are organized throughout the week.

Heden Centre is the heart of the Partille World Cup. This is where the information and tournament headquarters are located, from where large parts of the tournament are controlled. It is located right next to the main game centre Heden. It is a large meeting place where players can meet old and new friends, meet their comrades off the pitch and socialise with participants, leaders and the public, partillecup.com/the-centers.

The finals

The finals day are the obvious conclusion of a week filled with great handball, lots of people, nerves and emotions. For a few, the dream comes true and they can raise the trophy in front of the many spectators. The finals are played at Fristads Arena at Heden, with a capacity for thousands of spectators. Free entry. partillecup.com/en/the-finals.
excerpt: The largest handball tournament in the world is held in Gothenburg.

title: Göteborgsvarvet 2027
content:
The course – a 21 kilometres experience

Be part of the world’s largest half marathon!

The Göteborgsvarvet course winds through the festival-filled Slottsskogen park, along the scenic quays of Hisingen and past the buzz of Avenyn. The running party is further fuelled by more than 200,000 spectators, around 50 music stations and plenty of other uplifting activities along the route. Everyone is welcome to watch the race along the course, it’s free of charge. Read more about the Göteborgsvarvet course.

About Göteborgsvarvet

From 1,800 registered runners in 1980 to the world’s largest half marathon – a lot has happened over more than 45 years. Who has won, and which milestones have shaped the race over the years? Looking for results? Explore the results archive, History of Göteborgsvarvet.

Family Area

In addition to the 55,000 runners taking on the course, Göteborgsvarvet also bring the joy of running to our youngest participants at the Family Area. Here, you’ll find two exciting Minivarvet courses, along with plenty of fun activities, entertainment, delicious food and sweet treats for the whole family.

You’ll find the Family Area between Björngårdsvillan and Villa Belparc. Göteborgsvarvet Family Area.
excerpt: On May 22, Göteborgsvarvet returns, 21 kilometres of running and a world-class city celebration that spreads joy to both runners and spectators.

title: Way Out West 2027
content:
One of Europe’s best festivals takes over Slottsskogen city park!

Since 2007, the music and film festival has drawn visitors from across Sweden and far beyond, filling Gothenburg and Slottsskogen with unforgettable experiences. It is a must for every music-loving, culture-minded young minds.

The programme includes a line-up of Swedish and international acclaimed stars. It also offers film premieres, great vegetarian food, which is just as carefully curated as its music line-up, and a robust club programme called “Stay Out West” that takes place at night in central Gothenburg. WOW Talks is Way Out West’s own forum for talks and discussions. Here, thinkers, politicians, researchers and creatives come together to explore some of today’s most important issues from the stage in Slottsskogen.

Blind Bird tickets for 2027

A limited number of Blind Bird tickets are now on sale via the festival website. More information about artist announcements and other news will be released during the autumn. Keep up to date with the latest artist news on Way Out West’s website and social media channels – see the links on the right.

About Way Out West

Since its launch in 2007, Way Out West has welcomed artists such as Prince, Charli XCX, Erykah Badu, Kendrick Lamar, Florence + The Machine, Neil Young, Fred again.., Tame Impala, Alicia Keys, Chappell Roan, Frank Ocean, Robyn, The xx, Patti Smith, Solange and The Cure, among many others. The three-day, multi-genre festival takes place in Slottsskogen, a large park in the heart of Gothenburg. From here, much of the city is within walking distance, while trams, buses and ferries provide easy access to destinations across Gothenburg.

Sustainability has been a central focus of Way Out West since the festival was launched in 2007. Environmental and social responsibility are integrated into many aspects of the event, with ongoing efforts to reduce its impact and contribute to a more sustainable future.
excerpt: On August 12–14, 2027, Slottsskogen city park will once again come alive with three days of music, festivities and culture.

title: Gothenburg Horse Show with FEI World Cup™ Finals 2027
content:
From March 22–28, the 2027 edition of the Gothenburg Horse Show takes place at Scandinavium. Throughout the week, spectators can enjoy top-level equestrian sport combined with show elements and entertainment, making it a much-loved event for both dedicated horse enthusiasts and those less familiar with the sport.

Gothenburg welcomes home the FEI World Cup™ Finals 2027

FEI World Cup™ Finals in jumping, dressage, and vaulting are coming to Gothenburg and Scandinavium in 2027! Gothenburg Horse Show and the FEI share a long history, and it is with pride and joy that Got Event once again has once again been entrusted with hosting the World Cup Finals in 2027. 2027 also marks the 50th anniversary of the Gothenburg Horse Show, which makes this occasion extra special. 

Tickets and opening times

General ticket sales begin on October 8, 2026.
Times are subject to change. Please check the website before your visit.
Admission is free on the opening day, March 22, but a ticket is required.

Please note that there are no Gothenburg Horse Show events on March 23, and EuroHorse opens at 13:00 on March 24.

About Gothenburg Horse Show

Gothenburg Horse Show is one of the world’s leading indoor equestrian events and has been held annually since its start in spring 1977. Over three million horse lovers have visited the event over the years. The competitions are organised by Got Event AB on behalf of the FEI (the International Equestrian Federation) and the Swedish Equestrian Federation, in collaboration with the EuroHorse trade fair at the Swedish Exhibition & Congress Centre.
excerpt: Expect a true celebration of horses and spectacular competition days as the world’s best riders and an enthusiastic audience fill Scandinavium.

title: Gothia Cup 2027
content:
The world’s centre for youth football

Every summer, Gothenburg and its surrounding areas become the world’s meeting place for youth football. This is where the world’s largest international youth football tournament is played, with teams and players coming from all corners of the globe. What makes Gothia Cup unique is its diversity. The tournament brings young people together regardless of religion, skin colour or nationality. Football is the common language, helping to build understanding, friendship and memories that last a lifetime.

A city-wide festival in Gothenburg

For one exciting week, Gothenburg is filled with energy, colour and life. Around 35,000 players and almost as many accompanying guests fill the city and nearby towns. Gothia Cup can be seen and felt everywhere – on football pitches, in the streets and in public spaces. Visitors and local residents alike can enjoy a unique mix of football, music and culture from all over the world.

The centres

Heden and Kviberg are the largest field areas, both in terms of the number of pitches and their capacity for attendance. These are the venues where international youth football is played at the highest level. Throughout the week, partners host activities, competitions and entertainment across the event areas for visitors to enjoy, gothiacup.se/centers.

Tickets and entry

Entry is free to all matches during the tournament week. Tickets are only required for the Gothia Cup Opening Ceremony and the finals at Gamla Ullevi, one out of three arenas on the day of the finals. Please visit Gothia Cup’s website for ticket release information.

The opening ceremony will be held at Ullevi, gothiacup.se/opening ceremony.
Read about the finals here, gothiacup.se/finals.
excerpt: Gothia Cup is the world’s largest and most international youth football tournament with playing fields in and around Gothenburg.

title: Eurohorse 2027
content:
EuroHorse has everything for anyone passionate about horses – this is where the equestrian celebration truly comes to life. Around 80,000 visitors attend each year, all sharing a common interest in horses and equestrian sport. EuroHorse is one of the year’s major highlights, attracting enthusiasts from across the country.

Experience action-packed demonstrations in the arena, including western riding, Icelandic horses, dressage, horsemanship, police horses and much more. Browse a wide range of equestrian equipment and learn more about breed associations, breeding and the Swedish horse industry.

The Training Paddock

A brand-new training paddock made its debut at EuroHorse in 2026.. Gothenburg Horse Show and the exhibition have been closely connected since 1992, and the collaboration is now deepened through a new training arena. This initiative gives visitors the opportunity to get closer to the riders and horses and experience preparations behind the scenes. Training schedules are available at eurohorse.se/paddockprogram.

Ticket information

If you hold a ticket to Gothenburg Horse Show, admission to EuroHorse on the same day is included. You may visit the exhibition at any time during the day, regardless of whether you have a daytime or evening ticket for the competitions. If you wish to visit EuroHorse only, separate admission tickets are available.
excerpt: Northern Europe’s largest meeting place for horse lovers – EuroHorse returns to the Swedish Exhibition & Congress Centre in Gothenburg, March 24-28 2027.

title: Christmas Carols in the City – Julsång i City
content:
“Now a Thousand Christmas Candles Are Lit” or “Silent Night”?
Which is your favourite in this grand Christmas carol sing-along?

Christmas Carols in the City promises a warm festive spirit beyond the commercial buzz. That was exactly the intention when it all began back in the 1960s – Bo Eek, who still leads the singing, was a young priest then and one of those who wanted to highlight the rich tradition of Christmas music and its message, rather than the shopping frenzy surrounding the Cathedral. A message just as important today, in a world that needs sustainability more than things.

Come along and rehearse, so you can sing at home with family and friends! Choirs and musicians will guide you. Songbook with sheet music and lyrics is free, and entry is free of charge.
excerpt: Come and join in singing carols and hymns of the season, together with choirs and musicians!

title: Christmas market at Stora Holms Säteri
content:
When Stora Holms Säteri is dressed in its winter finery and the lights are lit across the courtyard, that special Christmas feeling fills the air. Here, tradition and togetherness meet in an atmospheric Christmas market that for many marks the true beginning of the festive season.

Stora Holms Säteri is delighted to welcome you visitors to a weekend filled with Christmas joy and tradition, as the estate once again opens its doors for the Christmas market – a tradition now approaching its 50th year.

You can enjoy genuine Christmas spirit while browsing and shopping for food and treats, crafts, art, flowers and much more from local producers.

Free admission.

title: Gothia Cup Innebandy 2027
content:
Gothia Cup Innebandy is one of the world’s largest and most international youth floorball tournaments. Every year, around 500 teams from eight nations take part, with more than 1,300 matches played across over 30 arenas.

Opening Ceremony at Scandinavium with an SSL Match

Gothia Cup Innebandy is more than just matches – it’s about meetings. Meetings between teams, cultures, and people, big and small, planned and spontaneous. The highlight of the week is the opening ceremony: a spectacular show filled with music, dance, and the presentation of all participating nations. When Scandinavium is packed with 10,000 spectators and the atmosphere reaches its peak, the entire floorball world comes together to share the joy.

Spectator Information

Admission is free to all matches and finals.
For match schedules and venues, please visit the Gothia Cup Innebandy website.
Matches are also streamed live – purchase your All Access Pass: Gothia Cup Innebandy Livestream.

Since 1994

Matches and human connections have been at the heart of Gothia Cup Innebandy since 1994. The tournament is about development, playing against teams from other countries or regions, and having fun – whether in the stands or on the court. Every match creates memories that last a lifetime, regardless of the result.
excerpt: A week filled with meetings and youth floorball.

title: Knippla Christmas market
content:
This year’s Christmas market takes place on December 5. Local artisans exhibit their work among the charming boathouses by the harbour, offering everything from homemade treats to crafts and Christmas wreaths.

Over the years, the popular Christmas market has grown into a beloved tradition. Visitors come to shop for fresh seafood delicacies, admire beautiful handicrafts, or enjoy a cosy fika indoors.

Look for Santa!

Meet by the fire station at 16:00 and join the search for Santa, who will be listening to the children’s Christmas wishes.

For travel information, check Västtrafik’s travel planner to get to Burö ferry terminal, from where you can reach Knippla.

title: CHL – Frölunda HC 2026/2027
content:
After another CHL title in the 2025/2026 season, Frölunda is back to defend its crown – and the journey begins in the group stage.

With five Champions Hockey League titles, Frölunda is the most successful club in the competition since its inception in 2014. Now the next chapter is written as Europe’s top teams gather once again, and Gothenburg becomes the stage for international top-level hockey.

The group stage offers fast-paced action, exciting matchups, and the chance to see Frölunda compete against Europe’s elite on home ice. Take your seat in the stands, experience the atmosphere, and be part of the journey from the very start as the pursuit of another CHL title begins.

title: Göteborg Film Festival Prisma 2026
content:
On October 23, the red carpet is rolled out as this year’s Prisma gets under way with the premiere of Julián, a colourful story about finding your own voice and having the courage to be exactly who you are.

Then there are films from around the world, pyjama cinema, singalongs and plenty more. At Bio Roy and Filmstaden Göta, you can discover new favourites on the big screen, while at Stadsbiblioteket you can try your hand at animation, creating film music, make-up, crafts and much more! But Prisma doesn’t stop there. Nordstan and Alingsås will host free cinema screenings during the autumn break, with even more film experiences taking place across the Västra Götaland Region.

Autumn break cinema – tickets on sale now

Bring your family, your friends, your favourite cuddly toy – or just yourself! See the programme and tickets on the Göteborg Film Festival website.

About Göteborg Film Festival Prisma

Göteborg Film Festival Prisma is a festival for young film lovers, celebrating its 16th edition this year. The festival for children and young people is an initiative by Göteborg Film Festival, bringing quality films from around the world to young audiences while also inspiring them to create films of their own. Prisma is also a fun and welcoming event featuring a variety of formats, guests and experiences.
excerpt: The 2026 festival is packed with films, giving the whole family the chance to discover exciting stories from around the world.

title: Halloween at Liseberg Park 2026
content:
Thrilling rides and hair-raising scares

During Halloween at Liseberg, cosy autumn atmosphere meets spine-tingling scares. Encounter magical woodland creatures in Sagoskogen (the Fairytale Forest), meet mischievous rabbits in Kaninlandet or venture into the darker parts of the park – if you dare.

Frightfully good fun

A mighty autumn storm has swept through Liseberg, bringing a little bit of everything with it! Thankfully, the rabbits are just as green, soft and cuddly as ever. And in Sagoskogen, the friends welcome those who are just the right size – and brave enough – to meet both fairies and trolls. As for all the park’s rides and attractions, they are just as much fun as ever.

Hair-raising scares

During Halloween, secrets and terrifying creatures lurk in the shadows. If you dare to enter the park’s dark scare zones, or its even darker haunted houses, nerve-racking experiences await to give you a real fright.

Halloween at Liseberg opens on October 2, while Autumn in Kaninlandet opens on September 26. During Autumn in Kaninlandet, only the rabbits’ own area is open.

Subject to change, please check Liseberg’s website for the current opening hours.
excerpt: Halloween at Liseberg runs from October 2 to November 1, 2026, and is a popular autumn break attraction for children and adults alike.

title: Christmas at Liseberg Park
content:
Sweden’s largest Christmas market at Liseberg

During Christmas at Liseberg, five million Christmas lights twinkle among around 2,000 Christmas trees. Throughout the park, you’ll find several Christmas markets with different themes and settings, from a wintry Nordic atmosphere with ice skating to an old-fashioned Christmas with beautifully decorated market stalls.

At the Tyrolean Market, an Alpine atmosphere takes over with après-ski, spiced drinks and an impressive Christmas pyramid as its centrepiece. In Santa’s Village, the pace is different, as the Christmas elves prepare for the big day and invite visitors of all ages to join in playful activities. Add winter rides, festive flavours and plenty of atmospheric settings, and there are many reasons to stay long after darkness falls.

Tickets on sale in October.

More information to be announced later. Subject to changes, please check the opening hours on the link before your visit.

Experience the atmospheric Christmas in Haga and Tredje Långgatan!

title: Advent at Nääs Castle and Christmas market
content:
Historic Advent weekends at Nääs Castle

  • November 28–29
  • December 5–6

Christmas market

Time: 11:00–16:00.
In and around the old stable, close to Kaffestugan and Slottsboden, you will find a small, carefully selected range of exhibitors offering arts and crafts and locally produced food. Exhibitors vary between the two weekends.

Guided Christmas tours of the house

Experience the unique interiors and festive atmosphere of Nääs Slott, beautifully decorated for Christmas. During the guided tour, you will hear about the history of Nääs and Christmas traditions of the past, and see the magnificent Christmas tree in the hall, decorated in period style. Tickets are limited and advance booking is recommended. In Swedish, see the ticket link in the right-hand column.

Mulled wine in the historic kitchen

Time: 11:00–16:00.
Warm up with a glass of glögg, Swedish mulled wine, served by maids and footmen in the historic kitchen.

Kaffestugan

Time: 11:00–16:00.
Enjoy rice pudding, Christmas sandwiches and Advent coffee in the cosy Kaffestugan next to Nääs Slott. Here you can experience the food culture of the turn of the 20th century in an authentic rural setting. Both the food and baked goods are inspired by what might have been served at Nääs in the late 19th and early 20th centuries.

Slottsboden

Time: 11:00–16:00.
Find thoughtful Christmas gifts at the cosy Nääs Slottsbod, housed in the old granary next to the house. The shop offers both new items with a nostalgic feel and a selection of antiques.

Horse and carriage rides

Time: 12:00–15:00.
Enjoy a horse-drawn carriage ride through the grounds.

Traditional Christmas music and St Stephen’s procession

Enjoy traditional Christmas music and period songs performed by Nääs Julkör.

Dancing around the Christmas tree

Join in the traditional dancing around the Christmas tree in front of the house, with festive fun for children and adults alike.

Christmas adventure for the whole family

Time: 11:00–15:00.
In the outdoor Christmas Adventure at Nääs Slott, children and adults can work together to find Christmas sacks hidden around the grounds before setting off in search of Father Christmas himself, where a Christmas present awaits. You may even encounter the slightly mischievous Christmas goat, who considers himself the true star of Christmas. Maps can be purchased from Slottsboden and include a Christmas present from Father Christmas.

Organised by August Abrahamsons stiftelse / Nääs Slott in collaboration with Näässamfundet and partners.
excerpt: A Christmas experience filled with festive scents, music and old-fashioned charm awaits at Nääs. Enjoy the simple pleasures, beautiful surroundings and festive atmosphere – just a short journey from Gothenburg.

featuredmedia.alt_text: Nääs Castle at dusk in a snowy landscape.

title: Improv Comedy Club – English
content:

title: The Gothenburg International Science Festival 2027
content:
This year’s festival theme is Hope and Play

A popular science festival for curious minds of all ages! Every year, the festival brings together science, inspiration and fresh perspectives to create a unique meeting place. The public programme offers lectures, debates, workshops, shows, discussions and much more. Discover everything from fun, thought-provoking activities that spark children’s curiosity to fascinating lectures by world-leading researchers.

The festival covers a wide range of scientific disciplines and attracts an average of 40,000 visits each year, making it one of Europe’s leading popular science events. Each year, the festival’s scientific advisory board selects a theme that runs throughout the festival and inspires its participants. The theme for 2027 is Hope and Play.

The International Science Festival Gothenburg offers both a public programme and a school programme. The public programme is free and open to everyone, while the school programme must be booked in advance by teachers. Visit the festival website to find out more and explore the full programme, which will be available from late February.

Public programme, April 22–25 – free and open to everyone

The programme features more than 100 exciting events covering everything from physics to psychology. The festival is committed to making science free and accessible to everyone. Even venues that normally charge admission offer free entry during the festival.

Most activities do not require tickets or advance booking unless otherwise stated. All you need to do is bring your curiosity and come along! Places are available on a first-come, first-served basis.

The full programme will be available on the festival website from late February. Events take place at various locations in and around Gothenburg, including Stadsbiblioteket at Götaplatsen and Contrast Public House on Tredje Långgatan.

School programme, April 12–23

The festival’s school programme gives preschool and compulsory school pupils and their teachers the opportunity to take part in fun, thought-provoking and creative activities. Covering most school subjects, the programme brings together a wide range of scientific disciplines.

Participants from universities, businesses, organisations and associations share a common goal: to introduce children and young people to the world of science. The programme includes interactive workshops, experiments, activities exploring values and attitudes, guided visits, performances, discussions and much more.

Activities for pupils take place both in person in Gothenburg and online.

The school programme must be booked in advance. It will be available on the festival website from early February.

The International Science Festival Gothenburg actively works with sustainability across several areas. Read more on the festival’s sustainability page.

.
excerpt: The International Science Festival Gothenburg is Sweden’s largest celebration of knowledge, offering exciting workshops, experiments, lectures and other fun ways to explore science. The public programme is completely free and open to everyone!

title: Gothenburg Book Fair 2027
content:
For four days, authors, researchers, cultural figures, industry professionals and visitors come together at Göteborg Book Fair. The programme includes seminars, author talks, book signings, exhibitors and a wealth of events for anyone looking to discover new perspectives, meet contemporary authors and take part in conversations about literature, culture and society.

There is also plenty for children and young people to discover, with activities and programme events designed to inspire a love of reading and curiosity.

All this and much more awaits during four inspiring days at the Swedish Exhibition & Congress Centre.

Göteborg Book Fair 2027

More information about Göteborg Book Fair 2027, including this year’s themes and programme, will be announced at a later date.

About Göteborg Book Fair

Göteborg Book Fair is the Nordic region’s largest cultural event and one of Europe’s largest book fairs. It brings together industry professionals and the general public around literature, culture and current social issues. The fair is a hub for discussion, inspiration and new perspectives, and works to promote learning, reading and the role of literature in society.
excerpt: Every September, Göteborg Book Fair returns to Gothenburg, transforming the Swedish Exhibition & Congress Centre into the Nordic region’s largest meeting place for literature, knowledge and culture.

featuredmedia.alt_text: Visitors on the exhibition floor at the Gothenburg Book Fair.

title: Hönö Klåva Christmas Market
content:
Christmas spirit for all ages in Hönö Klåva

During the Christmas market, the harbour comes alive with festive cheer and lots of fun for the whole family. Shop in Christmas-decorated stores, meet Santa, take a short boat trip around the harbour or join a quiz walk with the chance to win great prizes. There is also a dedicated children’s Christmas market with plenty of activities. All this and much more awaits at Hönö Klåva Christmas Market!

Free admission.

Join the M/S Kungsö round trip

Take the archipelago boat from Stenpiren, Eriksberg or Klippan to the Christmas market! Enjoy the beautiful views of the archipelago and have a coffee on board before immersing yourself in the scents, flavours and atmosphere of Christmas. End the day with a lovely boat trip back to the mainland. The journey takes about one hour. For timetable and tickets, see Styrsöbolaget.
excerpt: During the Christmas market, the harbour is bustling with life with lots of fun activities for both young and old.

title: Göteborg Vin & Deli 2027
content:
Experience the best wines and delicacies in the world and enjoy both old and new favorites at the fair Gothenburg Vin & Deli. The most knowledgeable suppliers are brought together for you to sample the flavours, try new styles, experience well-known brands and learn more.

Tastings

Gothenburg Vin & Deli has a full programme of drink tastings. The tastings take place in quiet, secluded tasting rooms where you get to taste several selected drinks from a certain manufacturer, or on an exciting theme.

Age limit

No visitors under 18 years are allowed at the fair, nor children in prams or carriers. ID check by the entrance.

title: En Öl & Whiskymässa 2027
content:
Regardless of your level of knowledge, En Öl and Whiskeymässa is perfect for those of you who want to discover all that is bubbling in the beer and whiskey world. As a beginner, you have a unique opportunity to try new styles and experience more brands. With over 2,000 different products to choose from, you can sample the flavours, and also get a nice introduction to the classic breweries and whiskey brands.

The fair attracts between 20,000-25,000 visitors annually. Over two days you can visit over 160 exhibitors, discover novelties, and learn more about beer and whiskey.

title: MyDOG 2027
content:
The Nordic region’s largest dog event 3–6 January 2027 at the Swedish Exhibition & Congress Centre in Gothenburg. Two dog shows and lots of other dog activities.

At the beginning of January every year, the entire Swedish Exhibition & Congress Centre is transformed into the Nordic region’s largest dog event. Over 9,000 dogs come to compete in two dog shows and most of the world’s dog breeds are represented in prestigious competitions.

While the competitions are taking place, lots of dog activities and exhibitions are also arranged. A packed programme is rolled out here with all types of activities such as police dog shows, dog theatre, lectures from the Nordic region’s leading specialists and much more.

Amidst all the activities and competitions, there is also a wide and unique range of all types of dog products, where all visitors can shop and update their accessories.

Opening hours

Every day 09:00–approximately 17:30.
MyDOG opens at 07:00 am but activities and exhibitions do not start until 09:00. Keep in mind that there will be fewer dogs exhibiting after 15:00. The show closes when the finals are finished, which is usually around 17:30.

Cashless

The Swedish Exhibition & Congress Centre is a cashless facility.
excerpt: Welcome to the world of dogs! MyDOG is the largest dog event in the Nordic region – the meeting place is a paradise for dog owners, dog lovers and anyone who wants to learn more about dogs.

featuredmedia.alt_text: A grey poodle in front of a red velvet curtain.

title: Lights in Alingsås 2026
content:
The theme

On October 2, Alingsås Energi will inaugurate the 27th edition of Lights in Alingsås on the theme Stories of Love. The theme explores love in all its forms — from the great epic romances we read about in books to the love we feel for family, friends, and our pets.

The Light installations

Lights in Alingsås is a lighting design event in which lighting designers from across the globe illuminate urban environments together with international students through a workshop. The workshop lasts for one week and ends with the grand opening. The installations can be seen throughout the month of October.

The trail

The installations will be spread out along a 3.5-kilometre walk starting in Åmanska Park and the city centre, continuing down to Nolhaga Park via Lugnet. On the way back toward the city centre, guides and visitors will pass Sävevägen before heading out along Södra Ringgatan.

In addition, several other installations (“highlights”) will be created locally or brought in from elsewhere, all inspired by this year’s theme of love.

Experience on your own

Walking and seeing the installations on your own is for free. The installations are lit from dusk to dawn and follow the usual streetlights’ rhythm every day from October 2 to November 1. From 24:00–05:00 the installations are programmed on “night-scene”, which means they are turned off or are not lit as strong.

To find out more about this year’s installations and event, download the Lights in Alingsås app from AppStore or Google Play. In the app you can also find a digital guided tour (audio-guide) for free that is available in Swedish or in English.

Book a private guided tour

To book a private guided tour in English, please see the Lights in Alingsås website. You can also join a public guided tour in Swedish. Tickets availble at Billetto.se from September 1. Both the lighting trail and the guided tours will start in Åmanska parken (Bryggaregatan 2).
excerpt: A unique light festival in the city centre of Alingsås.

title: A spine-chilling autumn break at Alfie Atkins Cultural Centre
content:
Meet Alfie Atkins in our daily theatre performances and explore a changing program of storytime, creative activities and other family-friendly events. Check our program calendar to see what’s on during your visit.

Exhibition

While you are visiting, take the opportunity to visit the studio where parts of Gunilla Bergström’s studio are recreated. Here you can see original furnishings, prizes and awards as well as curiosities.

The Centre in Gothenburg is full of activities related to culture, children’s development and rights. At the Alfie Atkins Cultural Centre, everyone is welcome to take part in activities that are included in the entrance fee. You need to book a time slot, even if you already have an annual pass or pre-purchased ticket. Buy and book your tickets on the website.

title: Kunskap & framtid
content:
Kunskap & framtid is the largest job and education fair in western Sweden, attracting thousands of high school students, college students, parents, and teachers to the Swedish Exhibition and Congress Centre every year. Here, you can find answers to everything related to studies, jobs, the labor market, study financing, studying abroad, and career planning.

At kunskap & framtid, you can get tips, advice, and contacts for future choices of education and career, whether you are motivated or tired of school, determined or lost, home-loving or adventurous. Here, you can meet universities and colleges from all over the country, vocational schools, employers, organizations, providers of study abroad programs and international universities.

Hammer has been GöteborgsOperan Danskompani’s biggest audience success ever, performed to euphoric sold-out performances both here at Göteborg Opera and around the world on the company’s international tours.

title: Volvo Scale Models – Through the Years
content:
Bert-Jan Nijhuis, who has collected Volvo scale models for over 40 years, has been the curator of the exhibition. The exhibition is a unique opportunity to witness Volvo’s history through the eyes of a true enthusiast.

From the first ÖV4 and the beautiful PV654, to the first aerodynamic PV36 Carioca, together with the very popular PV444, the very rare P1900 and the most popular 200 series. All the way to the XC60 and the newest EX90. The history of the other Volvo vehicles is not forgotten!

Busses and trucks from Volvo’s history are lined up together with the yellow construction vehicles.

There is also be a selection of Volvo sports vehicles, from the PV rally cars from Grus Kalle to the modern S60 WTCC race car driven by Thed Björk.

Location: Floor 2.

Free admission.

Different opening hours may occur on public holidays and in connection with long weekends, see more information here: Plan your visit, World of Volvo.
excerpt: For the first time, experience Volvo’s 98-year history in one place. This exhibition of scale model vehicles at World of Volvo showcases over 100 crafted Volvo scale models, each telling a story of innovation and design.

title: Native American Fashion
content:
Through four themes, the exhibition explores craftsmanship, traditions, symbols, materials, techniques, and identities among Indigenous peoples of North America. The journey spans from early European contact with Indigenous design and fashion to resistance, activism, and the restoration of traditions—while also looking toward the future, firmly rooted in the past.

For many designers, a major driving force is demonstrating that Indigenous peoples still exist despite colonization, oppression, and predictions that their cultures would disappear. The exhibition highlights a diversity of voices and perspectives from both Canada and the United States.

Traditions live on.

Native American Fashion opens with a celebration on April 11, 2025, and will be on display until November 2, 2026.
excerpt: The World Culture Museum opens a space to encounter Native American styles and traditions, moving between history, the future, and the present. You will meet fashion from streetwear to high-end, with rarely seen historical regalia in an exhibition that challenges stereotypes.

featuredmedia.alt_text: A women in Native American fashion

title: The Magic Flute
content:
The powerful Queen of the Night rules a realm of freely-flowing imagination – but her daughter Pamina has been kidnapped by their enemy, Sarastro. The stranger Tamino plunks down in the margins between the Queen’s and Sarastro’s opposing kingdoms – determined to help Pamina reach her independence. Along the way, he is aided by the eccentric Papageno, a set of magic chimes and an enchanted flute.

But who is truly good, and who is evil?

Mozart’s eternally youthful music balances playfulness and depth. Die Zauberflöte contains some of opera’s most iconic melodies—from the Queen of the Night’s dazzling aria to Papageno and Papagena’s playful duet, and Sarastro’s rumbling words of wisdom.
excerpt: A blend of comedy, drama, animation and delightful music bring to life this fantastic journey through darkness and light, as Tamino sets out to find his Pamina.

featuredmedia.alt_text: Poster the magic flute

title: Past the point
content:
”Enchanting choreography” (Aftonbladet)
”A wealth of movement and emotion” (Göteborgs-Posten)
”Worth the standing ovations” (Svenska Dagbladet)
”Frenetically fascinating” (Borås Tidning)

Cold Song

Creation by Marcos Morau

This piece by Spanish choreographer and multi-artist Marcos Morau is wildly entertaining with moments of absurd humor. The title Cold Song refers to the music, which is based on an aria of the same name from Henry Purcell’s opera King Arthur. In Cold Song the dancers take on different characters. The set consists of a mysterious table-like box that hides all sorts of fantastic surprises. Both the dancers and the set are transformed as Cold Song transports the audience somewhere between reality and theatrical magic. Such is the reputation of Marcos and the dance comapny that the piece was booked sight-unseen by several European tour locations even before it had its world premiere in February 2026.

Music in Cold Song

Original music by Ben Meerwein & Alex Röser Vatiché, inspired by Henry Purcell’s “Cold Song”.

Original recording “What power art thou? (Cold song)” from King Arthur, or The British Worthy (1691), Act 3.

Andreas Scholl, Accademia Bizantina, conductor Stefano Montanari. ℗ 2010 Decca Music Group Limited.

We Made a Mess!

Creation by Botis Seva

The rising British star Botis Seva creates intense dance experiences. He blends hip hop, breakdance and theatricality with contemporary dance to create a completely unique movement language – that is both poignant and ferocious – backed by pounding rhythm and deep empathy. We made a mess! is the choreographer’s first work for the GöteborgsOperans Danskompani, and was inspired by schoolyard power struggles. In spring 2025, Botis Seva and his company, Far from the norm, were guests at the Göteborg Opera’s Dance Festival with BLKDOG, which won an Olivier Award in 2019.
excerpt: Last season’s hit Past the point returns to the Main Stage, a double-bill with one piece by hip hop trailblazer Botis Seva and the other by Marcos Morau, Tanz’s “Choreographer of the Year” for 2025.

featuredmedia.alt_text: dance performance

title: Twelfth Night Concert and Ball
content:
The evening begins with an entertaining quiz concert, led by Måns Nilsson – a comedian, TV host, and one half of the popular comedy duo Anders & Måns. Enjoy the music while answering Måns’ questions on subjects both highbrow and light-hearted.

After the concert, the Main Stage is transformed into a ballroom, complete with a Viennese ensemble and then a swing band. On the dance floor you’ll see costumes, tuxedos, full-length silk gowns, little black dresses and tailored suits. Dress in whatever you find beautiful.

If you’d like to top the evening with something delicious either before or after the concert, the restaurant, Opera Bar and cafés offer a variety of menus. Most food options must be booked in advance.
excerpt: A festive opera concert with a music quiz together with opera singers, the Göteborg Opera Orchestra, and comedian Måns Nilsson. And of course, ball-dancing on the Main Stage – a tradition since 1995.

title: Slakthuset Saturdays – an Urban Farmers’ Market
content:
On the last Saturday of every month, the businesses in Slakthuset are joined by artisan friends from the surrounding area. Here you meet producers and creators directly — no retailers or middlemen. Expect an elevated market experience with the chance to eat and drink well on site, while browsing everything from handmade cheeses and specialty coffee to seasonal vegetables and exciting drinks to take home. You can also explore local artists and craftspeople, while being sustainably savvy by shopping vintage and second-hand.

Food and drink on site are available from visiting food trucks and from Cityysteriet, Spike Taproom (in collaboration with Mackbaren), Kafferäven, Mugwort BBQ and Wine Mechanics.

title: Seal spotting on board M/S Kastor
content:
The seals are to be found all year round in the Gothenburg archipelago. If not to hard wind,  they can be found on a rock. About 95% chance for this. Dolphins and orcas also possible but rare. After some days of hard wind the atlantic birds drift close to the coast and they are lovely to see.

A short and popular tour for all ages. 

Information

Departures from Hönö Klåva harbour, Hönö.
Duration around 1 hour.

After the tour, there is time to enjoy something to eat at one of the harbour’s fifteen restaurants.

title: Kulturnatta – Culture Night 2026
content:
Kulturnatta is a festival created by everyone, for everyone. Anyone can organise a programme event, while theatres, galleries, artists’ studios, cinemas and cultural venues across the city stay open into the evening. Explore everything from dance and theatre to themed walks, studio visits and workshops. Most activities are free of charge.

The full programme is scheduled to be released on September 18 at kulturnatta.goteborg.se.

Times

Kulturnatta does not have one fixed start time. Individual events begin at different times throughout the afternoon and evening, depending on each organiser. Many activities start around 17:00 or 18:00, while others begin later, such as 19:00 or 20:30.

Admission

Some workshops may charge a small fee for materials, while individual organisers may charge an admission fee. These fees are usually reduced or simply cover the costs involved. Any charges will be clearly stated in the official programme.

About Kulturnatta

For more than 30 years, Kulturnatta has brought together Gothenburg’s cultural community for one special evening each year. Organised by the City of Gothenburg in collaboration with the independent cultural sector, the festival showcases a wide range of art and culture, making it accessible to everyone and contributing to an open and inclusive city.
excerpt: Discover something new at Gothenburg’s city-wide celebration of arts and culture.

featuredmedia.alt_text: Illustration for Kulturnatta on a black background.

title: Autumn holiday at Maritiman
content:
Autumn break adventure in realm of shadows

Are you ready for a secret mission? During the autumn break, riddles, secrets and spy adventures await at Maritiman.

Join Maritiman’s very own spy inside the Realm of Shadows exhibition. With a spy booklet in hand, children will solve riddles and take on exciting challenges along the way. They will need to be observant, curious and clever! The Autumn Break Adventure takes place twice daily, at 12:15 and 14:45.

Between spy missions, there is plenty more to discover. Explore Maritiman’s historic ships, carry out your own experiments in Tim’s Ocean Lab, listen to stories with the audio guide and join ship tours, storytime sessions and in-depth guided tours exploring life both above and below the surface.

The autumn break also marks the grand finale of the season. Sunday November 1 is Maritiman’s final opening day of the year before the museum closes for the season – so don’t miss your last chance to come aboard for one final adventure!

Read more about the autumn break programme at Maritiman here.
excerpt: The autumn holiday at Maritiman offers fun activities for the whole family.

featuredmedia.alt_text: A blonde girl is looking out the window.

title: Laura Pausini
content:
Gothenburg will welcome one of the most successful artists of our time as Laura Pausini makes her long-awaited debut in the city. The Italian singer, who has sold over 75 million albums and is the only Italian artist to have won a Grammy Award, is renowned for her powerful live performances that captivate audiences worldwide.

The concert at Scandinavium will be part of her new world tour, coinciding with the release of her album IO CANTO 2 / YO CANTO 2. On stage, Pausini will deliver a unique mix of new interpretations, timeless classics, and her greatest hits from three decades.
excerpt: For the very first time, global superstar Laura Pausini is coming to Gothenburg. On November 21, 2027, she will take the stage at Scandinavium with her new world tour, offering the audience an exclusive concert experience.

featuredmedia.alt_text: Press photo, Io Canto World Tour. Laura stands behind dark landscape and gray sky, holding a flag with the text Io canto World tour

title: Anders Ekborg – A Silent Christmas
content:
For anyone who has ever experienced Anders Ekborg’s A Silent Christmas, it is no surprise that he is so closely associated with the holiday season. With a rich repertoire of songs and stories, he weaves together tradition and personal expression into a concert experience that reaches far beyond the music itself. For many, his voice and presence are synonymous with peace and warmth at Christmas.

Anders Ekborg needs little introduction in Sweden. Having triumphed in landmark musical productions such as Kristina från Duvemåla, Chess på svenska and Såsom i himmelen, as well as numerous films and television roles.

What may be less widely known is that he has performed close to 1,000 concerts as a soloist in Sweden and abroad over more than 30 years.

With a voice that reaches deep into the soul and a stage presence that captivates, Anders Ekborg is not only a singer and actor but also a true interpreter of the joy and spirit of Christmas. For this year’s edition of what has become a cherished tradition for so many, A Silent Christmas, Anders Ekborg once again embarks on a nationwide tour.
excerpt: A Silent Christmas is more than just a concert. It is a heartfelt tribute to the season’s message of love, togetherness and hope.

featuredmedia.alt_text: Anders Ekborg

title: Exhibition Landshövdingehus 150 years
content:
A historical architectural heritage

The Museum of Gothenburg presents a new exhibition about the landshövdingehus or county governor’s house in English, which is a unique part of the city’s architectural heritage. The exhibition will open in November 2025 and marks the 150th anniversary of these iconic buildings.

The exhibition will provide an insight into the history and significance of the house type. Through photographs, films, models and objects, visitors will have the opportunity to explore how the houses have shaped Gothenburg’s cityscape and culture.
excerpt: Celebrate Gothenburg’s iconic houses and discover more about one of the cities most famous houses type.

featuredmedia.alt_text: Landshövdingehus, colored postcard

title: Christmas Market at Gunnebo House and Gardens
content:
Gunnebo House and Gardens, just south of Gothenburg, a traditional Christmas market awaits in a historic setting. On 14–15, 21–22 and 28–29 November, visitors can browse handicrafts, Christmas gifts and locally produced food at one of Sweden’s best-preserved 18th-century estates.

Stalls can be found in Gunnebo’s shop, carriage house and carpentry workshop, as well as outdoors in the new kitchen garden. Find unique Christmas gifts for the whole family while enjoying Christmas songs and festive entertainment.

Then pause for a traditional Swedish Christmas fika with glögg, gingerbread and saffron buns (‘Lussekatter’) from the estate’s own bakery.

Free entry.
excerpt: During the Christmas season, Gunnebo House and Gardens fills with local crafts, seasonal flavours and Swedish Christmas traditions.

title: Djuren i staden – Animals in the city
content:
The exhibition invites you to meet gossiping sparrows, peek into rats’ tunnels, and discover the city’s secret inhabitants as they ride the tram, sneak through the park, or feast on cinnamon buns.

An exhibition filled with humour, knowledge and wow-facts – for children and adults alike. And suddenly, the city might look just a little bit different.

Plan your visit

Many people want to visit the sparrows, foxes and rats in Animals in the City – that is why we allow visitors in smaller groups, so that everyone has a good experience. You therefore need to book a time slot before your visit.

Booking a ticket

Booking a ticket for Animals in the City is done on the same day, directly at the museum. You book your time slot when you buy your ticket or show your annual pass at the museum. You will then receive a physical ticket that you can hand in to the host on site at the exhibition. Admission is every quarter of an hour and a visit lasts approximately 45 minutes.

We want everyone to have time to discover, explore and learn in peace and quiet – and the exhibition will remain on display for a long time, so you will have time to come back again! The exhibition will be open until January 9, 2028.
excerpt: The exhibition is inspired by Sarah Sheppard’s popular children’s book.

title: Ghostly Tales for Christmas
content:
As winter settles over Gothenburg, GEST opens its doors to something a little spookier.

Join them for an evening of classic yuletide ghost stories, tales where the warmth of the season meets the chill of the unknown. Inspired by the British tradition of reading ghost stories at Christmas, they’re telling tales that are quietly unsettling, strangely familiar, and perfect for long winter nights.

Step in from the cold, take your seat, and hold on tight.

Location: Karl Johansgatan 88, Göteborg.
excerpt: Ghostly Tales for Christmas is haunting Gothenburg this Holiday season.

featuredmedia.alt_text: 46 A vague face is visible through a dark window.

title: à la London Christmas Design Market
content:
Discover Scandinavian design

On November 20–22 and November 27–29, the design market à la London takes over the iconic old  building in central Gothenburg, gathering 150 incredible designers each weekend. Step into a vibrant world filled with everything from cutting-edge fashion and statement accessories to striking art and contemporary interior design.

This is your chance to meet the creators behind the brands and shop directly from independent designers and artists with fresh, bold ideas—passionate people who design to bring beauty and style into your everyday life. The best part? An new lineup of designers steps in for the second weekend. That means almost double the design, double the fun, and twice the reason to visit us twice! On top of that, you can dive into creative workshops, treat yourself to a cozy Swedish fika, and hunt for unique vintage treasures. Free admission!

A Christmas Market with a Modern Twist

This is not a traditional Christmas market. À la London offers a curated selection of small-scale, sustainably produced gifts, with a focus on design and distinctive products. The concept is aimed at customers looking for unique and thoughtfully designed gifts during the holiday season.

Since 2010, à la London has been a platform for innovative and unique design within fashion, art, and interior decor. Through its design markets, à la London aims to highlight and support design talents as well as small, creative businesses.

à la London in English

Free admission.
excerpt: Two weekends of cutting-edge design from 150 designers per weekend. The stunning old Casino fills with design, fashion, art and interiors. Perfect for finding local, unique, sustainable and wonderful Christmas gifts.

featuredmedia.alt_text: View of the design market and the visitors

title: Christmas Market at Tjolöholm Slott
content:
Over three weekends, the grounds of Tjolöholms Slott are filled with exhibitors, crafts, food, activities and entertainment for the whole family. Discover a carefully selected range of exhibitors in a historic setting, surrounded by the castle, estate and beautiful countryside.

The market offers crafts, local products, delicacies and festive flavours – from unique Christmas gifts to treats to take home for the Christmas table. There is also plenty to experience beyond the market stalls.

Meet Father Christmas and Mrs Christmas, take a horse-drawn carriage ride around the grounds and enjoy music, entertainment, beautiful choral singing and other activities. As darkness falls each market day, an atmospheric fire show lights up the winter evening.

If you fancy a break, there are plenty of options for food and refreshments. Stop by the café for something warm and tasty or choose from the market’s food trucks.

As dusk falls, the Christmas lights illuminate the grounds and give the market a completely different atmosphere. It is worth allowing plenty of time for your visit – there is lots to discover, taste and experience.

Tjolöholms Slott welcomes you to three weekends filled with crafts, festive flavours, traditions and Christmas cheer!
excerpt: The Christmas market at Tjolöholms Slott has been a festive tradition since 1987. This year, the market returns with Christmas lights, exhibitors, music, children’s activities, Father Christmas and much more.

featuredmedia.alt_text: Tjolöholm Castle in winter splendor at dusk

title: Christmas market Nääs Fabriker
content:
Between the historic brick buildings, local producers and exhibitors come together with crafts, delicacies, design and carefully selected Christmas gifts. Stroll among the market stalls, explore our shops, and enjoy something delicious, with Sävelången and the surrounding nature just steps away.

Throughout the weekends, the area will also come alive with Christmas music, choir performances and activities for visitors of all ages. Take a break with something warm to drink, sit down for a bite to eat, or make a full day of your visit and discover more of what Nääs Fabriker has to offer. A Christmas market celebrating craftsmanship, local producers and the history of this unique place.

Free admission.
Parking is available at Nääs Fabriker (SEK 60 for the full day).
excerpt: The Christmas market at Nääs Fabriker has become a cherished tradition, and this year Christmas will take center stage to an even greater extent. For the first time, the historic factory setting by Lake Sävelången will host the Christmas market over three weekends of Advent.

title: Challenge your mind at Paradox Museum Gothenburg
content:
Experience the Infinity Well, where you’ll appear to fly into an abyss, and the Zero Gravity Room, where you can float like an astronaut. Check out The Paradox Sofa to challenge your perception of reality and step into the Paradox Tunnel, where walking straight becomes a mind-bending challenge.

Every exhibit is designed to inspire and challenge your imagination, pushing the boundaries of creativity and perception. Behold the impossible, challenge gravity, and interrogate the essence of reality as you engage in an immersive escapade unmatched!

About Paradox Museum Gothenburg

The Paradox Museum is an innovative venue that combines the world of science, art and human perception. With over 40 amazing, paradox-inspired exhibits the museum offers more mind-twisting, eye-tricking experiences than any other edutainment destination in the world! You will learn everything about the exciting science behind paradoxes, have a ton of fun and take photos so spectacular that your friends will not believe they’re real.

Practial information

The museum offers time slots that you can book in advance. When booking your ticket, you choose the date and time that suit you best. The Zero Gravity Room requires an additional ticket.

All ages are welcome. If you are under the age of 15, you must be accompanied by an adult. Free admission for children under 4 years.

At paradoxmuseum.com/gothenburg, you’ll find answers to the most frequently asked questions.

Opening hours are subject to change.
excerpt: Step into Paradox Museum Gothenburg – where nothing makes sense yet everything feels real.

title: Cantorum’s Advent Concert in Vasakyrkan
content:
Cantorum welcomes you to an atmospheric Advent concert featuring a male choir and soloists at Vasakyrkan – a tradition spanning more than 40 years. The 45-strong Cantorum male choir takes centre stage, while the audience is invited to join in well-known hymns accompanied by organ and trumpet, alongside performances by soloists and choir.

A traditional Advent atmosphere awaits in the beautiful setting of Vasakyrkan.

title: Pre-Christmas market at Krokslätts Fabriker
content:
On November 7, the area fills with exhibitors and artisan food producers offering everything from sheepskins, cheeses and ceramics to handmade jewellery, knitted mittens, hand-dipped candles, arts and crafts and freshly baked saffron buns.

The market stretches from Restaurant Tegel to Hotell The Weaver. Browse for your first Christmas gifts, enjoy festive treats and soak up the atmosphere as the Christmas season gets under way.

Free admission.
excerpt: The fires are lit, the mulled wine is warming and Krokslätts Fabriker is filled with festive cheer. Enjoy a cosy Christmas market in the historic factory setting and get an early taste of Christmas!

title: St. Lucia and Christmas concert at Oscar Fredriks kyrka
content:
Enjoy the festive atmosphere at Oscar Fredriks kyrka with a traditional Lucia and Christmas concert. Oscar Fredriks Ceciliakör lights up the church with its Lucia procession, accompanied by Oscar Fredriks Kammarkör and Sinfonietta. Beautiful choral and orchestral music blends traditional and contemporary pieces, ranging from the solemn to the joyful.

Tickets for all four concerts go on sale via Billetto on October 12 at 10:00.

Doors open 30–45 minutes before the concert begins.
excerpt: Experience the magic of Lucia in one of Gothenburg’s most iconic churches.

featuredmedia.alt_text: Lucia and her attendants in the church.

category_heading: Traditional St. Lucia and Christmas concert

title: Mega flea market in Partille arena
content:
The Mega Flea Market at Partille arena is West Sweden’s largest indoor flea market, featuring more than 400 sellers and around 4,000 visitors throughout the day. Discover everything from clothing and vintage items to collectables, interiors and one-of-a-kind bargains – a full day of fun for the whole family.

In 2026, the event will take place on November 22 and in 2027 on  January 31 and March 7, from 10:00 am to 15:00. The arena is located just a few minutes from Partille Station, making it easy to reach by public transport.

.
excerpt: Hunt for bargains or sell your own treasures at the Mega Flea Market in Partille arena. Over 400 stalls filled with antiques, retro items, clothes, décor and unique finds.

featuredmedia.alt_text: View over the market place with a lot of people

title: Christmas Market in Kvarnbyn
content:
The market offers a wide range of local crafts and unique Christmas gifts. Browse everything from handmade jewellery and textiles to woodcraft and ceramics. There are also local delicacies to sample, including Christmas sweets and baked goods.

There will also be entertainment and activities for both children and adults, including music as well as crafts and workshops for younger visitors.

Practical information

The Christmas market in Kvarnbyn takes place around Götaforsliden on the first weekend of Advent, November 28–29. Götaforsliden is a street stretching for around 280 metres from Norra Forsåkersgatan to Royens gata.

Parking is limited during the market, so visitors are encouraged to use public transport where possible. From Gothenburg Central Station, take tram 4 or 12 towards Mölndal and get off at Mölndals innerstad. From there, it is around a 15-minute walk to Götaforsliden and the Christmas market in Kvarnbyn.

Free admission.
excerpt: Enjoy the festive atmosphere in Kvarnbyn! The market features a wide range of exhibitors, while several businesses in the area will also be open with their own programmes.

title: The Refreshments – Rock ’n’ Roll X-mas
content:
Expect upbeat, dance-friendly Christmas euphoria: festive favourites and their own material – all served with a rock ’n’ roll twist. Think traditional carols shaken up with a hint of Chuck Berry or Elvis.

This is the 24th year The Refreshments hit the road with their rock-inspired Christmas tour, always with special guests. This year’s line-up promises the perfect match: Svenne Rubin, frontman of the band bearing almost the same name, and the brilliant accordionist Anders Larsson.

Fast, fun and full of groove – a Christmas concert with real swing in its step.
excerpt: Fed up with slow Christmas ballads, jingling bells and the same old tunes you’ve heard a hundred times before? Then it’s time for a full-on Rock ’n’ Roll X-mas with The Refreshments – joined by Svenne Rubin and accordion king Anders Larsson.
