title: Imperial Triumphant + Knoll
content:
Describing Imperial Triumphant as the sound of New York – the true feel of New York – is not only apt, but also incredibly fitting, as the city’s chaotic energy, pulsating decadence and deafening grandeur permeate every album the trio has released. With 2025’s Goldstar, they managed to focus that energy to a whole new level – something that you will now finally get to experience on stage in Gothenburg again, Sunday 22 November.

Live, Imperial Triumphant is extreme, unique and visually striking – just like the city they love. And to really make sure that the very foundations are shaken, they have brought Knoll on tour.
excerpt: Imperial Triumphant is finally returning to Gothenburg again!

featuredmedia.alt_text: Poster for Imperial triumphant + Knoll

title: Westlife
content:
Over the course of their career, Westlife have achieved a remarkable number of milestones: more than 55 million albums sold, 36 number-one albums worldwide, and 14 UK number-one singles – more than any other artist aside from Elvis Presley and The Beatles. Their catalogue has been streamed over 3 billion times, and the band has sold more than 6 million concert tickets worldwide.

Their most recent tour, The Wild Dreams Tour, sold over 1.2 million tickets. Since reuniting in 2019, Westlife have performed more than 200 shows across 30 countries, cementing their position as the best-selling UK and Irish album group of the 21st century.

To mark the anniversary, the group are also releasing new music. The single “Chariot”, written by Ed Sheeran, Johnny McDaid and Will Reynolds and produced by Steve Mac, is a tribute to the fans and celebrates 25 years of music and memories.

“This year marks 25 years since we began this incredible journey together, and it still feels like the beginning. Our fans’ support has been absolutely amazing, and celebrating this with a world tour, new music, and a new album feels truly special. We can’t wait to see you all on the road and share this next chapter together.” – Westlife
excerpt: WESTLIFE 25: THE ANNIVERSARY WORLD TOUR. Expect an evening filled with the band’s greatest hits – from classic ballads to international chart-topping successes.

featuredmedia.alt_text: Poster for the music band Westlife

title: Ronnie Romero & Gus G – Trädgår’n Studio Live
content:
Ronnie Romero and Gus G have together built an incredibly impressive resumé, performing with some of the biggest names in hard rock. Ronnie has fronted legendary bands such as Rainbow and Michael Schenker’s group, while also releasing outstanding solo albums that truly showcase his powerful voice. Gus G is widely known for playing alongside Ozzy Osbourne, while continuing to lead his own band Firewind.

Get ready for an unforgettable night packed with massive rock hits and exceptional solo material — a true celebration of hard rock and heavy metal that no rock fan should miss!
excerpt: See Ronnie Romero and Gus G live in a powerful hard rock concert filled with classic rock anthems, heavy metal, and outstanding solo performances. An unforgettable evening for fans of Rainbow, Ozzy Osbourne, Firewind, and melodic hard rock!

featuredmedia.alt_text: Poster for Ronnie Romero and Gus G

title: Miles Davis Tribute
content:
Few artists have changed the direction of music the way Miles Davis did.

From the birth of cool jazz in the late 1940s, to masterpieces like Kind of Blue, and later into electric explorations with Bitches Brew – Miles Davis was never still. He constantly redefined jazz. Always one step ahead. Always in motion.

Kind of Blue remains the best-selling jazz album of all time. Milestones marked the beginning of something new. Together, they represent a turning point in music history where improvisation found a new language, and simplicity became depth.

This evening 100 years of innovation, edge, and beauty will be celebrated.

Trumpeter Samuel Olsson (Bohuslän Big Band) brings together some of Sweden’s leading jazz musicians to interpret music from Milestones and Kind of Blue:

Samuel Olsson – trumpet
Ludvig Broman – alto saxophone
Linus Lindblom – tenor saxophone
Carl Bagge – piano
Niklas Fernqvist – bass
Daniel Fredriksson – drums
excerpt: An evening where every note carries history, yet feels fully alive in the present.

featuredmedia.alt_text: Poster for Miles Davis 100 years

title: True Loves (US)
content:
An instrumental explosion of funk and soul that sounds like a block party in motion. Sweaty grooves, horn lines that lift the roof, and rhythms that make the whole room move.

Since forming in 2014, True Loves have grown from late-night jam sessions into a global live force. With millions of streams and acclaimed tours behind them, they’re known for a stage energy that is both razor-tight and completely loose at the same time. Professional, yet never stiff. This is music you feel in your body instantly.“The True Loves are simply one of the best bands in Seattle… It’s the soundtrack to that car chase you’ve always wanted to be in.”

– John Richards, KEXP“…a dreamscape of quick hits and neon lights…”

– Jake Uitti, KEXP

The band has released two acclaimed albums, Famous Last Words and Sunday Afternoon, and recently returned with new material through their latest singles. But the stage is where they truly belong.“Just being in their company and listening to them play is a special thing to behold.”

– Saundra Williams (Sharon Jones & The Dap-Kings)

This is groove at the highest level. No vocals needed – the instruments say everything.

More than just jazz. An intimate concert experience with world-renowned acoustics, outstanding food and drinks, and a dance floor that’s impossible to resist.
excerpt: Seattle-based True Loves are not just a band – they’re a feeling.

title: An evening with Priscilla Presley
content:
With “An Evening with Priscilla Presley,” Haga Concert Hall invites audiences to an exclusive evening where Priscilla shares stories from her life — from actress to businesswoman, and from author to executive producer of the biographical film Priscilla, directed and produced by Sofia Coppola and based on Priscilla’s book Elvis & Me.

Priscilla is also well known for her acting roles in Dallas and the comedy film The Naked Gun.

Priscilla (81 years old will, among other things, speak about her life with Elvis and her role as mother to Lisa Marie Presley, who tragically passed away in 2023. That same year, Priscilla Presley was approved to one day be buried in the Meditation Garden at Graceland alongside Elvis, Lisa Marie, and her grandson Benjamin Keough.

“It is a tremendous honour for us that Priscilla has chosen to come to Gothenburg and Haga Concert Hall

“It will be an evening to remember forever,” says the organizer Björkö SeaLodge Event AB.
excerpt: A unique opportunity you can’t miss, where Priscilla talks about her life and her life with Elvis. They remained friends until his death in 1977.

title: Swedish National Orchestra Academy
content:
Hear the orchestra from the 2-year international master’s program in symphonic orchestral performance at the Academy of Music and Drama. The program is unique in its kind and is conducted in collaboration with the Gothenburg Symphony Orchestra and the Gothenburg Opera.

Each academic year, the Swedish National Orchestra Academy produces eight orchestral productions. These involve internationally renowned conductors and soloists. Recently, Simon Crawford-Phillips, Jurjen Hempel, Vince Mendoza and Daniela Musca have been guests of the orchestra.
excerpt: Hear the orchestra of the University of Gothenburg master’s programme in symphonic orchestra performance.

title: Berliner Philharmoniker & Leif Ove Andsnes
content:
It will be one of spring’s absolute highlights when the world’s most famous symphony orchestra guest-performs at the Gothenburg Concert Hall for the first time in 30 years! The Berlin Philharmonic, led by chief conductor Kirill Petrenko, and star pianist Leif Ove Andsnes are welcomed. Together, they present a fantastic German-Norwegian evening, with two of the greatest works from Grieg and Beethoven, at the time of his anniversary.

Edvard Grieg’s Piano Concerto is a fundamental piece of Nordic classical music. He composed this central work when he was just 25 years old. Grieg adjusted the score for many years, but still retained parts and harmonies with a connection to the Nordic sound. And who better to interpret this music than the frequent guest of Gothenburg, Norwegian star pianist Leif Ove Andsnes?

The Pastoral Symphony is Beethoven’s sixth symphony and one of his best-known works. Beethoven was in an unusually light-hearted mood and wrote artful descriptions of each movement. We experience the thunderstorms, streams and birds, and finally the calm after the storm.

We are able to hear the Berlin Philharmonic in this concert thanks to the generous support of the Sten A. Olsson Foundation.
excerpt: The world’s most famous symphony orchestra performs in Gothenburg. Under the baton of chief conductor Kirill Petrenko, Berliner Philharmoniker and pianist Leif Ove Andsnes present Grieg’s beloved Piano Concerto.

title: Rocknytt Indoor 2027
content:
Rocknytt Indoor is proud to welcome legendary American singer and songwriter Geoff Tate to Trädgår’n in Gothenburg for a night that promises to go down in history.

As the original singer and frontman of Queensrÿche, Geoff Tate helped create some of progressive metal’s most iconic albums — including the masterpiece Operation: Mindcrime from 1988, a concept album still regarded as one of the genre’s most influential and acclaimed works.

Rocknytt Indoor proudly presents Swedish power metal force Civil War from Falun. Since their formation, the band has established itself as one of Sweden’s strongest names in modern power metal, combining epic choruses, heavy riffs, and grand arrangements that have captivated fans worldwide.

Sweden’s most beloved heavy metal machine is coming to Rocknytt Indoor 2027; Bullet!

After relaunching their career with the new album Kickstarter, Bullet is once again ready to do what they do best — deliver classic, uncompromising heavy metal live, loud, and hard. The band has evolved from cult favorites into near-national heroes.

Since the late 1990s, Swiss melodic heavy metal band Crystal Ball has built a strong reputation across Europe — yet, surprisingly, no Swedish promoter has ever brought them to Sweden before. That changes now.
excerpt: Rocknytt Indoor returns on 30 January 2027. On stage: Geoff Tate – Operation: Mindcrime, The Final Chapter, Civil War, Bullet, Crystal Ball and Saffire. The Rocknytt Award 2027 will also be presented during the evening.

title: STVW Punk Rave
content:
His signature sound – which he calls “Punk Rave” – blends high-energy electronic music with the melodies and emotion of pop-punk, emo, and rock. The result? A club experience where rave meets Warped Tour.

Live, STVW isn’t just behind the decks – he picks up the electric guitar on stage and turns his set into something that feels more like a rock show than a typical DJ performance. With his Punk rave Live  concept, sometimes joined by live drums, he blurs the line between club and concert. STVW has collaborated with names like Electric Callboy, Breathe Carolina, Timmy Trumpet, and Cheat Codes, and has released music on some of the biggest labels in the dance scene, such as Spinnin’ Records, Rave Culture, and Revealed Recordings.

At the same time, his PUNK RAVE reinterpretations have gained support from pop-punk icons like Simple Plan, blink-182, Good Charlotte, and Boys Like Girls, who have personally approved his explosive versions of their songs. After sold-out tour stops in the UK, Australia, Canada, and Germany, STVW is now taking his PUNK RAVE concept worldwide – and now he’s coming to Sweden for the first time.

If you’ve ever wanted to hear emo and pop-punk at rave tempo on a dancefloor – this is the night.

The night is presented by High 5ive Music, who have brought emo music to nightclubs across Sweden through their concept “Emo Club.”
excerpt: For the first time in Sweden: STVW – the DJ who transforms emo and pop-punk into rave. The German producer and DJ STVW (Steve Witzlsperger) is one of the fastest-growing names in the new generation of dance music.

content:
Weeping Willows embark on an extensive Christmas tour in December 2026. In recent years, the band’s Christmas concerts have established themselves as a much-loved and highly anticipated tradition, praised by reviewers as “the most beautiful Christmas concert of the year”.

The repertoire features carefully selected Christmas songs in the band’s own interpretations, alongside their original material – all chosen to reflect the many layers of Christmas, from melancholy and reflection to warmth and hope.

title: The 3 maestros – Zimmer, Williams & Morricone
content:
Experience the unforgettable works of Hans Zimmer (Gladiator, Inception, The Lion King), John Williams (Star Wars, Indiana Jones, Jurassic Park) and Ennio Morricone (The Mission, Cinema Paradiso, Once Upon a Time in the West, The Good, the Bad and the Ugly).

From epic Hollywood soundtracks to timeless classics: a musical experience guaranteed to give you goosebumps – performed by a large symphony orchestra.
excerpt: A unique symphonic concert awaits you. The greatest masters of film music united for one evening filled with emotion and immersive soundscapes.

title: La voix humaine & Metamorphosen
content:
Abandonment is one of the great human sorrows. Poulenc’s opera La Voix humaine describes just such a farewell, with the lead role performed by the Gothenburg Symphony’s Principal Guest Conductor Barbara Hannigan. She sings, conducts and acts. It is beautiful, painful and intimate.

With La voix humaine, Barbara Hannigan has created one of the most groundbreaking musical theatre works of our time. In this unique project, she leads the orchestra and the drama through live cameras on stage – and breaks away from the traditional boundaries between conductor, singer and actor in real time.

La voix humaine has become a milestone for the 2000s and is internationally acclaimed. Leading institutions continue to offer the production for new performances – a rare distinction for a contemporary opera.

Now Hannigan brings La voix humaine back to Gothenburg for a unique visit, confirming the central role of the Gothenburg Symphony in the project. The collaboration also results in a performance at the Oslo Opera House.

The return celebrates an ongoing artistic journey and a work that continues to resonate, evolve and challenge conventions – led by an artist who has fundamentally reshaped the actual performance language.

“I find myself asking if there even is an ex-lover? What and who really exists within these deep and true emotions of love, loss and loneliness?” Barbara Hannigan

The concert begins with Richard Strauss’ Metamorphosen, giving voice to 23 individual string instruments. The piece from 1945 is a memorial to human culture devastated by war. All that can save us now is divine intervention.
excerpt: Experience Barbara Hannigan as soprano and conductor in Poulenc’s renowned one-act opera. Hear the gripping performance about the last conversation between two lovers. As starter Strauss’ Metamorphosen.

featuredmedia.alt_text: a conductor

title: From A Great Height: A symphonic take on the music of Radiohead
content:
The border between indie rock and classical music is explored with the full power of the Gothenburg Symphony Orchestra.

May 21st 2027 marks 30 years since the release of the legendary album OK Computer, considered one of the most important rock albums of all time. Not least because it was a radical departure from the band’s earlier sound. “An album created in a world where the internet had yet to take off, it eerily prefigured the themes of alienation and information overload that everyone would start discussing the minute it did.” (The Guardian).
Here, listeners will find Radiohead’s magnum opus, Paranoid Android, which is musically comparable to Queen’s Bohemian Rhapsody.

Now the Gothenburg Symphony Orchestra takes on the massive soundscape that is OK Computer. In new arrangements collected by conductor Christoffer Nobin, we hear symphonic interpretations of songs like Paranoid Android, Karma Police and No Surprises. We also travel on through the entire musical spectrum of Radiohead’s world, encountering more hits with roots in indie rock and electronica.

British Radiohead is one of few bands that, for decades, has successfully merged groundbreaking musical evolution with huge hits, sold-out tours and chart-topping songs. In an age of mass-produced rock and pop, the band’s uncompromising artistic approach stands out like a a breath of fresh air.

Radiohead’s experimental approach to sound, form and instrumentation also pushes open the doors to classical music. What began as an indie band from Oxford has now become a creative universe. Guitarist Jonny Greenwood is an established composer of orchestral music and film scores, three times Oscar nominated.

This is a concert for those who love Radiohead in particular and rock music in general, but also for those who appreciate symphonic music  – not least with connections to contemporary composers such as Pärt, Penderecki and Messiaen. Bring a friend and experience the sound that continues to captivate generations, together with the Gothenburg Symphony Orchestra, vocal soloists, choir, organ and a stage band.

Creator, artistic director and conductor is Christoffer Nobin, who has previously produced several cross over art productions. Visuals, lights and production by Linus Fellbom, Sweden’s most acclaimed light designer and known for numerous pioneering projects in opera, theatre and dance.
excerpt: Enter the musical universe of Radiohead. 30 years after the release of the album OK Computer, the epic songs are given new life.

Every February, young orchestra musicians between 11 and 19 years of age gather at Gothenburg Concert Hall for the popular Sport Break Orchestra. The orchestra is not afraid to take on everything from music from films and video games to Bach, Carmen, or Shostakovich. This is their closing concert!

Care to join?

Read more and how to join in.

title: Kim Wilde – The Singles Tour 2027
content:
A hit-packed show filled with timeless classics from one of the most beloved songs.

With more than four decades on stage, Kim Wilde is one of the most iconic artists on the international pop scene. Together with her brother and songwriting partner Ricky Wilde and her band, she delivers energetic live performances that continue to captivate audiences around the world.

The hits you don’t want to miss

“The Singles Tour” features a string of classic hits, including:
Kids in America, Chequered Love, Cambodia, You Came, Never Trust a Stranger, Keep Me Hanging On, View From a Bridge — and many more.

An evening filled with nostalgia and energy

Experience one of the biggest pop icons of the 1980s live in a show where the hits take center stage — with the same power, emotion, and energy that have made Kim Wilde a favorite around the world.
excerpt: Pop icon Kim Wilde returns to Sweden with her long-awaited “The Singles Tour.”

title: Love is all
content:
An outpouring of love set to The Beatles’ music: we travel down Penny Lane with Lucy and Michelle, pause to listen to Blackbird, and are reminded that love is all you need. A concert bubbling with joyful energy, rising all the way to the third balcony.

Love is All is a tribute concert featuring hundreds of choral singers alongside musicians and soloists, all under the direction of Fredrik Berglund and Simon Ljungman. Fredrik and Simon the duo who previously appeared on the Main Stage with A Tribute to Simon & Garfunkel (2023), The Sound of Sweden (2024) and La-La-Laleh (2025).

“Beatles songs have shaped us as singers and musicians. We really look forward to singing them for (and with!) the audience and the choir. There’s a unique alchemy when hundreds of voices and The Beatles’ melodies unite, combining to create something truly special. We want everyone to share in that experience. It’s a joy to return to the Göteborg Opera and to bring together choral singers from across the region in a musical firework display.”

– Fredrik Berglund och Simon Ljungman
excerpt: Experience and sing along to the timeless songbook of The Beatles. Fredrik Berglund and Simon Ljungman present Love is all in collaboration with the Göteborg Opera.

featuredmedia.alt_text: choir singers on stage

title: One Fell Swoop Company – By a Thread
content:
Long ropes stretch through the air, wrap around bodies, and weave the acrobats’ movements into a living system of trust and precision. Here, every step carries meaning. Every movement sets something in motion. A single mistake can ripple through the entire ensemble.

Through breathtaking acrobatics and finely tuned choreography, you are invited into a world where the balancing act is not only physical, but deeply human. The performance moves seamlessly between playfulness and nerve-racking tension, reflecting the invisible threads that hold us together in our own lives.

By a Thread explores what it means to trust someone else — and to carry the weight of another person yourself. It is an intimate, visually striking experience about friendship, risk, closeness, and courage.

A reminder that it is in our encounters with others that we are truly tested. And where we grow.

With support from Kulturrådet, touring with Cirkusnätverket.

featuredmedia.alt_text: A man hanging on a rope from the ceiling

title: Dansbandsfestivalen
content:
The ambition is to create a recurring festival where dance bands take centre stage. Expect an evening filled with music, dancing, togetherness and unforgettable entertainment. This is only the beginning of what is hoped to become a beloved tradition for dance band fans from near and far.

Trädgår’n will gradually reveal this year’s artists, and can already announce the first confirmed band: Streaplers. A range of activities and experiences will also be presented, taking place both inside Trädgår’n and out on the large outdoor terrace.

Visit the website and social media channels for the latest updates about Dansbandsfestivalen.
excerpt: Trädgår’n makes history by hosting the very first Dansbandsfestivalen in Gothenburg.

title: Wallmans Christmas Dinnershow
content:
Gothenburg, are you ready for an evening that tastes a little better, swings a little more and sparkles a little brighter?

In 1991, Wallmans opened its doors in Stockholm, becoming Sweden’s first and leading conceptual dinner show experience. The original that laid the foundation for a concept now found across Scandinavia and enjoyed by millions of guests from around the world.

Now, as part of its 35th anniversary celebrations, Wallmans returns to Gothenburg for an exclusive guest appearance.

An evening at Wallmans is something truly special. From the moment you arrive, you are welcomed by the stars themselves. The performers – who also serve as your hosts for the evening – become your personal guides through a night filled with entertainment, excellent food and surprises. Between courses, expect everything from timeless classics to modern hits, all with a festive Christmas twist.

Throughout the evening, a carefully composed three-course menu is served, with each dish designed to enhance the experience. For dessert, Wallmans’ legendary sweet buffet awaits, with flavours that set the tone for the most festive time of the year.
excerpt: Forget the expected and step into a Christmas celebration beyond the ordinary. At Wallmans Dinner Show in Gothenburg, the festive season is transformed into a full experience where food, music and atmosphere come together – equally perfect for colleagues, groups of friends or a night out for two.

featuredmedia.alt_text: A man on stage with winged arms

title: Lars Winnerbäck
content:
For 30 years, Winnerbäck has brought Swedish melancholy to the stage, putting words to the emotions of an entire generation. Across fourteen studio albums, he has created a distinct and instantly recognizable voice, and even coined what might be the most Swedish word of all: tandläkarväder.

This autumn, Winnerbäck releases his new album Längtan till våren and embarks on a major arena tour together with his band:

Jonna Löfgren – drums
Jerker Odelholm – bass
Mikaela Hansson – piano, synth
Carl Ekerstam – guitar
Staffan Johansson – guitar
Sandra Widman – vocals
excerpt: This autumn, Lars Winnerbäck sets out on a major arena tour with a stop in Gothenburg on November 6. Joining him is his acclaimed live band, along with brand-new music for the audience to enjoy.

title: Morgan Jay: La Dolce Vita Tour
content:
Morgan Jay has quickly become one of the most talked-about names on the international stand-up scene, known for his unique blend of comedy, improvisation, and music. With millions of views across social media and appearances on MTV’s Wild ’N Out, NBC, and Comedy Central, he has built a global audience.

As a first-generation American with Brazilian and Italian roots, Morgan Jay draws inspiration from both his upbringing and his musical background. His live performances combine audience interaction, music, and spontaneous humor in a format that has made him a fan favorite.

In addition to stand-up, Morgan Jay has also appeared as an actor in several notable productions, including the Apple TV+ series Stick alongside Owen Wilson and Marc Maron.

Presented by: Live Nation.
excerpt: The Los Angeles-based comedian and musician Morgan Jay is coming to Sweden in spring 2027 with his La Dolce Vita Tour* He will perform at Draken Live in Gothenburg on March 13th.

featuredmedia.alt_text: Morgan Jay

title: An intimate Christmas with Tareq Taylor and Andreas Aleman
content:
Together with some of Sweden’s finest musicians, they create a magical Christmas evening filled with atmospheric ballads, swinging festive classics, humour and reflection.

Experience joy, warmth and depth during an evening where music and storytelling take centre stage.

Secure your ticket for one of the winter’s most personal and atmospheric experiences – an evening in perfect harmony.

Presented by Lifeline.
excerpt: You are invited into a warm and personal musical living room together with Andreas and Tareq.

featuredmedia.alt_text: Tareq Taylor and Andreas Aleman.

title: The Seasons in New Colours
content:
Fresh and captivating music for a celebration! The evening begins with celebrated pianist Rudolf Buchbinder, who is now back in Gothenburg. With magical hands, he plays Robert Schumann’s imaginative and only Piano Concerto. It reflects Schumann’s longing for his future wife.

Aziza Sadikova, Uzbek who resides in Berlin, has her own unique musical language. A Baroque spirit hovers over her rhythmic work Farbenzeiten, which is a paraphrasing of Vivaldi’s Four Seasons. Here, the well-known notes gain new colour and sparkle with poppy melodies. As soloists, we hear a quartet from the Gothenburg Symphony Orchestra. Like the premiere in 2024, this performance is led by Kent Nagano, former principal guest conductor of the Gothenburg Symphony Orchestra.

Highly regarded concert pianist Rudolf Buchbinder has met audiences from stages in South Africa, Finland, Japan, Mexico and everywhere in between. He is particularly appreciated for his interpretations of Beethoven’s piano works, to which he adds his own distinctive touch. Dazzling and imaginative!

Come closer

Have a seat in the Great Hall an hour before the concert and let the introduction open the door to the stories behind the works, facts about the composers and personal reflections. The introduction is included in your ticket, lasts about 30 minutes and has free seating in the hall.
excerpt: Hear a new take on Vivaldi’s energetic seasons and Schumann’s imaginative Piano Concerto. Conductor Kent Nagano leads the Gothenburg Symphony Orchestra together with acclaimed pianist Rudolf Buchbinder.

featuredmedia.alt_text: Conductor Kent Nagano

title: The Harlem Spirit of gospel By Anthony Morgan
content:
Experience the magic of authentic American gospel as The Harlem Spirit of Gospel Choir takes the stage! Led by the legendary Anthony Morgan, this eight-member ensemble delivers a vibrant concert filled with power, warmth, and musical joy. From beloved Christmas classics to uplifting gospel favorites, an unforgettable evening awaits—one that will raise the roof and warm your heart.

The choir’s members have performed alongside music legends such as Aretha Franklin, Diana Ross, Stevie Wonder, Alicia Keys, and Christina Aguilera. It shows. Every note, every movement, and every smile radiates pure passion. This is more than a concert—it is an experience that will stay with you long after the final song.

“Controversial, professional, energetic, inspiring, and full of spirit.”

That is how audiences have described Harlem Spirit of Gospel. Their voices move you, their energy is contagious, and their stage presence is truly extraordinary.

Welcome to an evening filled with celebration, hope, and heavenly song—a Christmas show that will leave you smiling long after the applause has faded.
excerpt: They are back at Stora Teatern – a dazzling Christmas and gospel show with Anthony Morgan! Direct from Harlem, New York, comes a Christmas spectacular that will make your soul dance.

title: Daniel Lemma – Morning Train 25 year
content:
The album will be performed in its entirety, something that has never been done before and will likely never happen again.

In addition to the songs from Morning Train, the evening will also feature a selection of other beloved favourites. It will be a personal and memorable journey back through the music, the stories, and the moments that have shaped us over the years.

Welcome to a special evening along Memory Lane.
excerpt: In 2026, the album Morning Train celebrates its 25th anniversary – and we want to celebrate it together with you. In a unique anniversary concert.

title: Seinabo Sey
content:
This autumn, she returns to the stage at Stora Teatern for a grand concert experience featuring both new Swedish songs and beloved favourites.

When “Younger” and “Hard Time” broke through, something shifted in the international music landscape. These were not just chart-topping songs—they were the arrival of a voice that entered the room and took possession of it. The deep, soulful tone of Seinabo Sey carried both authority and fragility, a presence and inevitability that felt impossible to ignore. In hindsight, it is difficult to imagine it unfolding any other way.

Yet it soon became clear that the boundaries of commercial pop were too narrow. Sey has always navigated by a different compass, and on the album The One After Me, this became more evident than ever. The tempo slowed, the voice was allowed to hover in a more meditative space, and the soundscape opened up toward something larger than the present moment: hints of Swedish folk music, a nyckelharpa emerging from the mist, and melodies unfolding slowly, as if searching for a truth beyond the immediate. It was an album unafraid to dwell in the unfinished, in cosmic searching, in the space between past and present.

On March 13, Seinabo Sey releases her fourth album, Välkommen hem—her most personal and poetic work to date, and for the first time sung entirely in Swedish. A linguistic choice that some might view as risky, but for her represents a deepening: a way of getting closer to what she truly wants to express, of shaping words in her own everyday language and allowing that vision to permeate every detail of the production.
excerpt: Seinabo Sey is back with new music and a major concert hall tour. With her new album Välkommen hem, she invites the audience into a personal and poetic universe where her unique voice takes center stage.

title: La Compagnia Finzi Pasca Titizé ‐ A Venetian Dream
content:
Titizé is a visually spectacular and poetic performance that takes the audience into a surreal universe filled with music, magic, acrobatics, and fleeting mirages.

The performance is created and directed by Daniele Finzi Pasca and combines the expressive language of Commedia dell’Arte with contemporary circus, dance, and music in a completely unique theatrical style. With floating acrobats, transforming masks, and a set design that captures the enchanting atmosphere of Venice, a sensorial and visual experience is created that speaks directly to the audience—regardless of age or language.

The title “Titizé”—“You are”—is a rhythmic and symbol-rich word that highlights the power of existence itself. The performance carries a universal sensibility in which body language, clowning, movement, and music together tell stories beyond words.

On stage are eleven extraordinary performing artists—acrobats, actors, and musicians—who transport the audience to the heart of Venice, where past and present merge into a seductive, dreamlike narrative.

Titizé is a visual feast for all the senses—a magical journey filled with wonder, lightness, and imagination.
excerpt: Welcome to a dreamlike Venice where reality and fantasy merge into a breathtaking circus experience.

title: Isabelle Demers: Organ music from past and present
content:
Hear two loves united through organ music. Although they were never a couple, Clara Schumann was the object of Johannes Brahms’ admiration throughout his life. At this concert, organist Isabelle Demers performs an organ variation by both of these composers.

Before the intermission, we get to enjoy works by some female pioneers of the organ world, including Rachel Laurin, the contemporary Canadian composer who passed away in 2023. Sara Wennerberg-Reuter, composer and organist in Stockholm, lived a century earlier. She is being featured this year at the Göteborg International Organ Festival.

Canadian Isabelle Demers is an organist above and beyond the ordinary: her technique is outstanding, and she is known for playing from memory – a phenomenal capacity that has made her an in-demand concert organist in the US and Canada. Now she is back for this organ concert that takes us on a journey through time and space.
excerpt: Organist Isabelle Demers performs in Gothenburg in a solo programme of female composers. Hear pieces by Clara Schumann, Elsa Barraine and Rachel Laurin from the 19th century to today.

featuredmedia.alt_text: An organ on the stage

title: Linda May Han Oh
content:
Outstanding bassist Linda May Han Oh has toured and recorded with stars like Pat Metheny, Kenny Barron and Terri Lyne Carrington.  Known for her intuitive and creative playing on both the double and electric bass, in 2022 the magazine JazzTimes named her Bassist of the Year.

Lyrical and rhythmic, yet endlessly varied on both the electric and double bass, she playfully moves between avant-garde, post-bop and jazz-funk.

Her name is on five critically acclaimed albums, including an album that won the Grammy for Best Jazz Instrumental Album in 2023. She has also composed music for indie films and classical works for small ensembles.

Joining her in Gothenburg is pianist Fabian Almazán, who is also her husband; he has developed his own approach to manipulating and electrifying the acoustic piano. Also on stage is drummer Mark Whitfield Jr., who is frequently the clear choice for musicians such as Kurt Rosenwinkel, Orrin Evans and Chico Freeman.
excerpt: With a hot name on the New York jazz scene, this superb bassist has toured with stars and makes music for films. Linda May Han Oh is coming to Gothenburg with her trio.

featuredmedia.alt_text: Linda May Han Oh

title: Songs of Hope and Joy
content:
Spirituality, humanism and symphonic magnificence. Under the baton of young French conductor Samy Rachid, the Gothenburg Symphony present three generations of composers from France, Sweden and Germany – Lili Boulanger, Elfrida Andrée and Felix Mendelssohn. Together, the work of these three composers forms an evening of prayer, manifesto and celebration.

The evening begins with Lili Boulanger’s Pie Jesu for soprano, organ and harp. It is a gripping and sincere farewell composed shortly before the composer’s far too early death. Next, we hear yet another female composer: one of Sweden’s pioneers of her time. Elfrida Andrée’s powerful Organ Symphony No. 2 was composed in the French symphonic tradition with Nordic clarity, and offers orchestral imagination and faith in the power of music.

The concert concludes with Felix Mendelssohn’s Symphony No. 2, called Lobgesang – a monumental work for orchestra, choir and soloists. Composed in honour of the inventor Gutenberg, this is a symphony that becomes a hymn. It is a tribute to mankind’s creative ability and, not least, to one of the era’s most powerful tools: the printed word.

The evening’s conductor is Samy Rachid, who is French and the assistant conductor of the Boston Symphony Orchestra, and who is now performing in Gothenburg for the first time.Come closer

Have a seat in the Great Hall an hour before the concert and let the introduction open the door to the stories behind the works, facts about the composers and personal reflections. The introduction is included in your ticket, lasts about 30 minutes and has free seating in the hall.
excerpt: An evening in the spirit of humanism. The Gothenburg Symphony Orchestra present three generations of composers in a magnificent evening of organ, choir and soloists. The finale is Mendelssohn’s spectacular Lobgesang.

title: To Broadway with Nils Landgren
content:
With a red trombone and a golden voice, Nisse Landgren is a long-time interpreter of Leonard Bernstein’s music. And now it is finally happening on the stage of the Concert Hall. In addition to music from the classic musical West Side Story, Landgren’s ensemble, with the expressive vocalist Ida Sand at the front, also present songs from On the Town, and the charged Mass.

We also hear a palette of other songs here by Kurt Weill, Cat Stevens, Joe Sample and Nils Landgren himself. They are all on the freshly released album Love of My Life, and as on the 2016 Bernstein tribute Some Other Time, the arrangements are by American composer Vince Mendoza. The reviews say: “Heavenly!”

Landgren’s supergroup includes none other than Lars Danielsson on bass, Joel Lyssarides on piano and Robert Ikiz on drums. The Gothenburg Symphony Orchestra is led by Sara Trobäck and Mårten Larsson. We promise that it will be hard to sit still.

Don’t miss Kulturnatta (Culture Night) in our foyer after the concert, with more music and mingling.

“Landgren’s humble joy and energy are contagious. And what notes his phenomenal air flow creates, both when singing and on the trombone – soft, sincere and masterful.” Lira Magazine

Friday night follows

Don’t miss Kulturnatta in the Götaplats foyer after the Friday concert with more music and meetings.

Come closer

Have a seat in the Great Hall an hour before the Friday concert and let the introduction open the door to the stories behind the works, facts about the composers and personal reflections. The introduction is included in your ticket, lasts about 30 minutes and has free seating in the hall.
excerpt: Sparkling sounds of jazz and musicals as superb trombone player Nils Landgren and his band join the Gothenburg Symphony Orchestra. Original compositions are woven together with Bernstein’s rich trove of songs for a concert of warmth and togetherness.

title: Angelic Voices from Bulgaria
content:
With crystal-clear voices and an age-old sound, world-renowned women’s choir Bulgarian Voices Angelite present an experience beyond the ordinary. Tight harmonies and hypnotic rhythms unite the Bulgarian folk tradition with timeless beauty.

Bulgarian Voices Angelite’s international range is impressive: they have performed on major stages in Europe, the US, Japan and India, and have sung at events such as the Nobel Prize concert in Oslo.

For decades, Bulgarian Voices Angelite were largely unknown, but years after the fall of the Iron Curtain, the singers enchanted the world with their mystical, nearly cryptic way of singing – distinctive rhythmic shifts, often dissonant harmonies, and without vibrato.

The Bulgarian choral phenomenon has established their own authentic style by finding inspiration from classical music and genres such as rock, jazz and throat singing (they have released several albums in collaboration with Mongolian Huun-Huur-Tu). At the same time, they have preserved their Balkan heritage, with tones infused with a timeless language.
excerpt: With crystal-clear voices, world-renowned choir Bulgarian Voices Angelite present an experience beyond the ordinary. Tight harmonies and hypnotic rhythms unite the Bulgarian folk tradition with timeless beauty.

featuredmedia.alt_text: Bulgarian Voices Angelite

title: Shabaka (UK)
content:
On Tuesday 13 October, we are proud to present one of the standout bookings of the year.

Shabaka is a musician who refuses to be confined by any single genre, expression or sound. As the bandleader of Sons of Kemet, he helped shake up London with politically charged fire, and with The Comet Is Coming he brought jazz to sweat-soaked dancefloors. At the height of his career as one of the most celebrated saxophonists of his generation, he made the unexpected move of putting down the saxophone entirely to begin a new chapter.

What we see at Nefertiti is an artist who has stripped back his own success in search of something deeper. His new voice is rooted in flutes, shakuhachi and ritual, a meditative, deeply personal sound world centred on breath, presence and transformation. It is both fragile and monumental, carrying a spiritual weight that places him in the lineage of artists like Alice Coltrane, Pharoah Sanders and Sun Ra.

To experience an artist of Shabaka’s calibre in such an intimate setting is rare. He is not coming to rely on past achievements, but because the music feels urgent and necessary right now.

Don’t miss one of jazz’s most visionary voices as he visits Nefertiti.
excerpt: When Shabaka Hutchings steps onto the stage at Nefertiti, it is more than a concert – it is an encounter with the architect behind the modern British jazz movement that has taken the world by storm over the past decade.

featuredmedia.alt_text: Shabaka

title: de clair.
content:
Behind de clair is singer-songwriter Clara Rudelius from Karlshamn, an artist whose strong yet vulnerable voice carries her music with rare presence. She started playing guitar at the age of ten and soon found her way to the old out-of-tune piano in her family’s living room. Early influences like Nico, Leonard Cohen, Bob Dylan and Björk later shaped her own writing and production.

The result is a subtle yet powerful sound: minimalist indie/alternative folk where fragile arrangements meet open, sometimes provocative lyrics about injustice, friendship, memory and love.

Her debut hiding mountains in the palm of my hand (2024) earned her the “Newcomer of the Year” award and international acclaim.
excerpt: After a busy touring year, de clair now returns with new music – live at Nefertiti on 9 November.

title: Finalloppet
content:
From 250 metres to 19 kilometres

On All Saints’ Day, Gothenburg Ski Club organises Finalloppet in the scenic Delsjö terrain.

The youngest participants can take on the 250-metre “Parvelbanan”, while older children and adults can choose from courses of 1.9, 2.3 and 5.3 kilometres. The 10 kilometres race forms part of the Gothenburg Classic, together with the events Hisingen Runt and Mölndal Open Water, while the 19 kilometres race is the official competition class.

All races start and finish at Skatås exercise centre.

Read more and register at finalloppet.com.

Spectators are welcome to attend free of charge and enjoy the atmosphere and enthusiasm of the participants.

Gothenburg Classic – Göteborgsklassikern

Finalloppet is part of the Göteborgsklassikern, together with Hisingen Runt (cycling) and Mölndal Open Water (swimming). Completing the Göteborgsklassikern means cycling 50 kilometres, swimming 1,000 metres and running 10 kilometres.
excerpt: Finalloppet is the largest cross-country race in Western Sweden and has been held annually since 1968. The event is open to the whole family and all age groups, with a variety of distances to choose from.

featuredmedia.alt_text: Runners in the forest.

category_heading: Running fun for the whole family

title: Myth and Mystery with Barbara Hannigan
content:
Barbara Hannigan has become inseparable from Ligeti’s Mysteries of the Macabre – the dramatically theatrical scene from the opera Le Grand Macabre, reimagined for the concert stage. Her fearless combination of razor-sharp virtuosity, physical comedy and total dramatic dedication transformed the piece into a modern classic. Filmed performances have travelled far beyond concert halls, attracting 100,000 views and introducing a new audience to György Ligeti’s wild fantasy.

The opera, which Ligeti composed with a premiere in Stockholm in 1978, was a farce about the end of the world. Now, more than a decade after the first performance in Gothenburg, Hannigan returns for this signature role at a unique concert event. It is a way to mark and celebrate her deep artistic relationship with the Gothenburg Symphony Orchestra.

This evening, Barbara Hannigan takes us on more bizarre adventures. To begin, we travel to an enchanted lake to the romantic sounds of Liadov, before seeker Claude Vivier depicts mysteries of the outer limits of the universe.

Béla Bartók’s raw story, The Miraculous Mandarin, explores the power of human passion. It is filled with a fierce and erotically charged atmosphere. Striking, barbaric rhythms and dissonance generate a frightening effect. But Bartók also had space for humour: coquettish clarinet solos and flirtatious trombones are heard during the seduction scenes.
Needless to say the premiere in 1926 was a scandal.

Come closer

Have a seat in the Great Hall an hour before the concert and let the introduction open the door to the stories behind the works, facts about the composers and personal reflections. The introduction is included in your ticket, lasts about 30 minutes and has free seating in the hall.
excerpt: Barbara Hannigan takes on Ligeti’s Macabre once again, which she made a modern classic. But first, Bartók’s erotic tale, Vivier’s journey through space, and a dazzling Haydn symphony. All with the Gothenburg Symphony Orchestra.

title: In the footsteps of Schoenberg
content:
Barbara Hannigan leads an inspiring and captivating programme circling around Arnold Schoenberg and some of his contemporary colleagues, exploring their significance to 20th century music. With her uncompromising presence, she takes us through a concert in which expressionism, modernism and the thrilling new sound-worlds of chamber music all converge.

Arnold Schoenberg was a true revolutionary, one of modernism’s most influential figures and a teacher of several great twentieth-century composers. His Lieder (songs), composed during the transition between the late-romantic period and early modernism, are presented here in arrangements by Danish composer Hans Abrahamsen, who has gently adapted them to an orchestral format.
Paul Hindemith studied under Schoenberg and developed his own sound, which can be heard clearly in his Kleine Kammermusik and Chamber Music No. 1, pieces in which tradition meets a modern form. Franz Schreker conducted several works by Schoenberg, and was well acquainted with his music. Schreker’s Der Wind is a golden piece for piano quintet from 1909. It reflects the expressive sound that inspired so many composers in Vienna around the turn of the last century.

We also hear exclusive music from the British-Iranian composers Golfam and Hooshyar Khayam, including a specially written new vocal work for Barbara Hannigan.
excerpt: Follow along on a journey through the 20th century, where thrilling modernism and contemporary sounds meet. Barbara Hannigan and musicians from the Gothenburg Symphony Orchestra present music connected to the innovative Arnold Schoenberg.

featuredmedia.alt_text: Barbara Hannigan

title: Beethoven Violin Concerto
content:
Beethoven’s only violin concerto did not gain renown until after his death. Now it is one of the most beloved. The soloist and orchestra are woven together in a lively discussion here. Popular Japanese violinist Akiko Suwanai has everything necessary for this virtuosic challenge.

As introduction, we hear a powerful piece that draws inspiration from Beethoven. Subito con forza is written by Unsuk Chin, one of Europe’s most noted female composers.

Composer Modest Mussorgsky was a prominent figure of nineteenth-century Russian music. He possessed a bold, raw sense of individuality which challenged the romantic tradition. He composed his “Pictures” in honour of an artist who had passed away.

The ten pieces of music take listeners down into the Parisian catacombs, to the hut of the witch Baba Yaga, and to marvel at a sketch of an enormous gate in Kiev (which was never built). Maurice Ravel took on the task of adapting the innovative piano piece into a challenging orchestral suite.

The young conductor Kahchun Wong was born in Singapore and explores both Eastern and Western legacies. He is chief conductor of the Japan Philharmonic Orchestra and also works with leading ensembles in Europe and the US. We now get to see him in Gothenburg.

Come closer

Have a seat in the Great Hall an hour before the concert and let the introduction open the door to the stories behind the works, facts about the composers and personal reflections. The introduction is included in your ticket, lasts about 30 minutes and has free seating in the hall.
excerpt: Experience two moving, boldly vibrant masterpieces: Beethoven’s Violin Concerto and Pictures at an Exhibition. Japanese violinist Akiko Suwanai is back with the Gothenburg Symphony Orchestra in the company of conductor Kahchun Wong.

featuredmedia.alt_text: Akiko Suwanai

title: A star encounter with Canellakis & Hadelich
content:
Two stars shine together in a journey ranging from playful to serious. Augustin Hadelich plays Bartók’s intense Violin Concerto under the baton of highly in-demand Karina Canellakis. To conclude, we hear Shostakovich’s dazzling final symphony, full of musical turns and a lifetime of experiencing artistry under political pressure.

Karina Canellakis is internationally acclaimed for her intensity and her ability to merge analytical clarity with an emotionally charged performance. Born and raised in New York, she regularly performs with leading orchestras in Europe and the US.

Augustin Hadelich is among today’s most frequently engaged violinists, acclaimed for his depth and brilliant presence. Bartók’s intense Violin Concerto is a test of skill that he is one of few violinists to have mastered.

After the intermission, Canellakis and the orchestra demonstrate their full register in Dmitri Shostakovich’s Symphony No. 15. The composer’s final symphony was his most enigmatic work. Playful musical quotations and sudden, serious outbursts create a multifaceted composition. A ticking sound in the music foreshadows that Shostakovich is in the autumn of his life. “Perhaps I am on my way elsewhere, but the music will last forever.”

Come closer

Have a seat in the Great Hall an hour before the concert and let the introduction open the door to the stories behind the works, facts about the composers and personal reflections. The introduction is included in your ticket, lasts about 30 minutes and has free seating in the hall.
excerpt: Highly in-demand conductor Karina Canellakis performs with the Gothenburg Symphony Orchestra with star violinist Augustin Hadelich. Hear Bartók’s intense Violin Concerto and Shostakovich’s masterful final symphony.

featuredmedia.alt_text: Karina Canellakis

title: Piano magic with Christian Zacharias
content:
With intimacy and elegance, Christian Zacharias presents a solo concert. In this programme spanning over three centuries, we hear music characterised by playfulness, depth and lyrical beauty – from the finesses of Haydn and Schubert, to the French sounds of Couperin and Poulenc.

Christian Zacharias is particularly associated with Haydn’s piano sonatas, with interpretations that highlight their humour, elegance and structural definition. Schubert’s Moments Musicaux represents a more inward-oriented and lyrical romance, while Domenico Scarlatti’s Sonata in C Minor is a concentrated and expressive piece with sharp contrasts and rhythmic energy.

However, the French theme is clear throughout the concert, with Francis Poulenc’s personal, often melancholy piano music, and François Couperin’s decorated Baroque pieces.

A particular gem is Poulenc’s Improvisation No. 15, a peaceful and heartfelt homage to Édith Piaf, with simplicity and emotional precision at the centre.

Come closer

Have a seat in the Great Hall an hour before the concert and let the introduction open the door to the stories behind the works, facts about the composers and personal reflections. The introduction is included in your ticket, lasts about 30 minutes and has free seating in the hall.
excerpt: Baroque gems and French esprit as Christian Zacharias presents a solo programme for piano. The music of Haydn and Schubert contain playfulness, depth and lyrical beauty.

featuredmedia.alt_text: Christian Zacharias

title: Family Concert: Children’s Christmas Celebration
content:
Christmas begins at Gothenburg Concert Hall. At this concert, the youngest audience members get to enjoy a cosy, starlit evening and hear the most beautiful Christmas songs. Bring the whole family for a festive concert featuring the Gothenburg Symphony Orchestra’s brass ensemble, singers and soloists.

Don’t be surprised if we all get to join in and sing some of the holiday season’s most beautiful songs together. A wonderful start to Christmas in a warm spirit of togetherness.

Tomas von Brömssen is our host.
excerpt: Bring the whole family and enjoy a cosy, starlit evening of the most beautiful Christmas music! A festive concert for all ages with the Gothenburg Symphony Orchestra’s brass ensemble, Tomas von Brömssen, choirs and soloists. From age 6.

featuredmedia.alt_text: poster with flowers and instruments

title: Vega Trails (UK)
content:
Led by bassist and composer Milo Fitzpatrick (Portico Quartet), Vega Trails returns with Sierra Tracks, inspired by his move to the mountains northwest of Madrid. The music blends chamber music, jazz, and folk influences, expanding from the intimate duo sound of their debut into a wider, more cinematic landscape.

Longtime collaborator Jordan Smart (Mammal Hands) brings saxophone, bass clarinet, and ney, joined by piano, vibraphone, and strings to create a richly layered sound world shaped by sweeping landscapes and twilight mountain light.

More than music, Sierra Tracks reflects on mental health and recovery from pandemic isolation, exploring how movement and nature can bring clarity and release.

“This album explores the relationship between our complex inner mental processes and how the natural world can help us find definition and clarity.” – Milo Fitzpatrick
excerpt: Experience a cinematic journey through Spain’s Sierra de Guadarrama with Vega Trails at Nefertiti.

featuredmedia.alt_text: Vega Trails

title: Little North (DK)
content:
With their upcoming album Crossing Currents on the acclaimed German label ACT Music, Danish trio Little North take the next step in their musical journey. Since 2020, they have released six albums and established themselves as a distinct voice on the European jazz scene.

Working as a collective, all three members compose and draw on a wide range of influences, with curiosity driving each release into new sonic territories.

Crossing Currents was created in New York with vibraphonist Joel Ross and saxophonist Hannes Bennich, blending Nordic lyricism with the energy of the international jazz scene.

In a live setting, the music expands further through collaboration with Dutch guitarist Reinier Baas, known for his rhythmic drive and melodic inventiveness, shaping the music in real time and making each performance unique.
excerpt: Little North’s music is created in real time, shaped by the interplay between musicians, space, and audience, building bridges between the Nordic and international jazz scenes.

title: Caoilfhionn Rose (UK)
content:
Built around piano, Caoilfhionn Rose’s sound sound weaves together synths, rhythm, saxophone, and atmospheric samples into something both grounded and ethereal.

With her third album Constellation (2024), she stepped forward as a distinctive voice, exploring nature, musical diversity, and the healing power of sound through an experimental and curious approach.

She has toured extensively across Europe, supporting artists such as Hania Rani, Alabaster DePlume, GoGo Penguin, and Bess Atwell, as well as performing her own shows. Collaborations, including the single Illusions with Danish duo Svaneborg Kardyb, have further shaped her evolving sound.

Now entering a new chapter as she works on her next album, Caoilfhionn Rose arrives at Nefertiti as an artist in constant motion—curious, exploratory, and deeply present in the moment.
excerpt: Caoilfhionn Rose moves freely between folk, jazz, and classical music, creating a dreamlike sonic world where organic textures meet electronic elements.

featuredmedia.alt_text: Caoilfhionn Rose

title: ULD (NO)
content:
ULD consists of Une Lorentze Onarheim, Lucia Andreadatter Utnem, and Dagny Braanen Lindgren. Their debut album fra en annen virkelighet (2024) led to three Spellemann Prize nominations in 2025, alongside wins of both the Edvard Prize and the Prøysen Prize. Their songs “Vondt å vende” and “Jeg skal finne deg” also charted in the Norwegian Top 50.

The trio has sold out major shows, including two concerts at Oslo Concert Hall, and their first Denmark tour. In 2026, they open for Aphaca in Copenhagen in front of 6,000 people over two nights.

ULD has performed at festivals such as Bergenfest, SPOT Festival, Tønder Festival, Piknik i Parken, and Union Chapel, and appeared at the Norwegian Royal Palace.

In summer 2026, they play festivals including Roskilde and OverOslo, followed by a Scandinavian tour including Iceland and London.

On stage, ULD is known for their calm, dynamic presence and use of silence as part of the music.
excerpt: With three voices, piano, and accordion, the trio blends folk, traditional song, alternative pop, and Nordic musical traditions into an intimate and precise sonic landscape.

title: High Pressure with Kullrusk
content:
The guiding star – even the god – in Kullrusk’s world is the doyen of electric jazz: trumpet player and saxophonist Eddie Harris. And his spirit is truly brought to life as these four plug in and press the “on” button.

Saxophone players Jonas Kullhammar and Per “Ruskträsk” Johansson are at the helm, joined by an equally rock-solid and fearless rhythm section: bass player Sven Lindvall and drummer Martin Jonsson. Together they are Kullrusk, a quartet that has held onto its distinctive personality from day one, consistently presenting a sound in which the electric saxophones go toe to toe with agile acoustic accompaniment.

This fiery music is filled with explosive funk, hard-swinging jazz – and everything in between. Music that knows no limits.
excerpt: Kullrusk is back! Jonas Kullhammar and Per “Ruskträsk” Johansson are plugging their saxophones back into a pair of amps. Full throttle, all-out, and jazzy rock are all words that describe this 60s-inspired, high-pressure sound.

featuredmedia.alt_text: Kullrusk

title: Mozart & Beethoven up close
content:
Musicians from the Gothenburg Symphony Orchestra join in for an effervescent chamber music programme during Advent. Works by Mozart and Beethoven demonstrate the development of the classical form from elegance and clarity to music in a larger format characterised by expansive and dramatic expressiveness.

Mozart’s Oboe Quartet from 1781 combines virtuosity with beautiful dialogue, and the oboe is given a lyrical and technically demanding role. String Quartet No. 14 in G Major, also known as the “Spring quartet”, is the first of Mozart’s six so-called Haydn quartets. It is known for its blend of various Baroque elements and the galant style of Classicism.

Beethoven’s three string trios mark his breakthrough as a chamber music composer at just 28 years of age. In the dramatic Trio in C Minor and the lighter Trio in G Major, he is already stretching the classical form and gesturing to the breakthrough of the string quartet and romantic style.

This warm evening offers a close encounter with the greatest icons of classical music.
excerpt: Hear Mozart’s effervescent Oboe Quartet and dramatic string trios from Beethoven. Musicians from the Gothenburg Symphony Orchestra present chamber music that moves from tight clarity to expansive romance.

featuredmedia.alt_text: Musicians from the Gothenburg Symphony Orchestra plays an instrument

title: Winter Organ with Johannes Landgren
content:
Versatile organist Johannes Landgren is joined by a trio on vocals, sax and percussion.

The entire palette of the organ is exposed in this programme in a kaleidoscope of sounds: Bach’s Toccata and Fugue in D Minor, Det är en ros utsprungen, jazz music by Duke Ellington for alto sax and organ, Christmas suite, romantic organ music by Otto Olsson and exciting improvisations.

We hear the delightful sound of soprano Helena Ek, and dramatic music for percussion with Daniel Berg. In addition, we hear songs by composer Karin Rehnqvist, whose rich oeuvre captures life’s essential challenges and values – always with a humanistic and ethical pathos.

In conclusion, we hear Czech modernist Petr Eben, who combines percussion with the full power of the organ in his Landscapes of Patmos.

We also hear Håkan Lewin on alto sax.
excerpt: A concert in the spirit of winter and Christmas, where the organ shines in all its richness – from Bach’s dramatic masterpieces to Christmas songs, improvisation and newly composed music.

featuredmedia.alt_text: An organ on stage

title: Víkingur Ólafsson and Herbert Blomstedt
content:
With many global successes to his name, one dream still remains for Víkingur Ólafsson: to perform with the great conductor Herbert Blomstedt. That dream is now a reality.

Piano virtuoso Ólafsson won a Grammy Award for Bach’s Goldberg Variations in 2025 and is the world’s most-streamed classical artist. The Gothenburg Symphony Orchestra is a favourite partner, and he now returns to interpret Mozart’s Piano Concerto No. 24.
It was just before the premiere of The Marriage of Figaro in 1786 that Mozart completed his Piano Concerto No. 24. It was an immediate success and greats such as Beethoven, Brahms and Clara Schumann held it in high regard.

After the intermission, we get to enjoy Brahms’ Symphony No. 4. Highly esteemed, Brahms composed his final symphony in the 1880s, perhaps the most sorrowful of them all. Don’t miss the beautiful flute solo in the final movement.
98-year-old Blomstedt has a special ability to convey details. Together with the orchestra, he gives this centuries-old music the precise shimmer it deserves.

We are able to hear Víkingur Ólafsson and Herbert Blomstedt in this concert thanks to the generous support of the Sten A. Olsson Foundation.
excerpt: The incredibly popular Víkingur Ólafsson is back with the Gothenburg Symphony Orchestra, this time with maestro Herbert Blomstedt. Experience a unique evening with Mozart’s Piano Concerto No. 24 and Brahms’ Symphony No. 4.

featuredmedia.alt_text: Víkingur Ólafsson

title: Víkingur Ólafsson plays Bach & Beethoven
content:
Thanks to Beethoven, piano music stepped out of private salons and into concert halls. With Víkingur Ólafsson, we understand why. The Icelandic star’s latest album, Opus 109, took off like a rocket on the classical music charts. Critics praise Ólafsson’s clarity and contrasts, how he plays with both substance and emotion.

The legendary Piano Sonata in E Major, Opus 109, was one of Beethoven’s most remarkable creations. Few works for piano have been granted so many analyses and individual tributes. The first movement resembles a contemplative dreamscape, before breaking out into a wild flow of energy. It all culminates in the third movement with a joyful meditation: like a music box, it approaches a deep stillness.

In addition we hear sounds from Schubert and J.S. Bach, which are lovingly presented by Ólafsson. Take this chance to discover the ingenuity and pleasure hidden within the works of the great masters with an international star at the piano.

“For those prepared to go along with him, Ólafsson opens up a transcendent vista on to a brave new world.”  – The Guardian

Come closer

Have a seat in the Great Hall an hour before the concert and let the introduction open the door to the stories behind the works, facts about the composers and personal reflections. The introduction is included in your ticket, lasts about 30 minutes and has free seating in the hall.
excerpt: Follow along to a dreamy landscape together with Icelandic star pianist Víkingur Ólafsson. The great masters of classical music are presented through a heartfelt selection from Ólafsson’s latest solo album, Opus 109.

featuredmedia.alt_text: Víkingur Ólafsson

title: Erik Söderlind & Lars Jansson Quartet
content:
Pianist Lars Jansson and guitarist Erik Söderlind have, over the years, developed an intuitive musical dialogue and a shared melodic language. Drawing on a range of musical “moments,” this collaboration has now resulted in thirteen original compositions that together form a cohesive whole.

“Why Does Rain Fall” is the title of the new album presented by Lars Jansson and Erik Söderlind during their performance in Linköping on August 12.

Those who have followed both musicians over the years will also recognize that Lars Jansson has, to some extent, taken on the mentor role once held by the legendary Kjell Öhman in relation to Erik Söderlind. At the same time, Söderlind himself has in recent years become both a mentor and an inspiration to a younger generation of jazz musicians. This development is reflected in a more mature and reflective tone in his already highly acclaimed guitar playing.

The Erik Söderlind & Lars Jansson Quartet features Paul Svanberg on drums and Olli Rantala (replacing Niklas Fernqvist) on bass.
excerpt: Erik Söderlind and Lars Jansson’s music spans the full spectrum, from driving bebop to romantic lyricism and introspective melancholy.

featuredmedia.alt_text: Erik Söderlind and Lars Jansson

title: corto.alto (UK)
content:
His debut album Bad With Names was nominated for the 2024 Mercury Prize and won Best Album at the Scottish Jazz Awards. In 2025, he followed up with Act Of The Year, winning the Jazz FM Audience Award and UK Independent Breakthrough at the AIM Awards.

Now signed to Ninja Tune, he has released a string of singles including Don’t Listen, Vandal and April feat. anaiis, blending jazz, club music, hip hop, soul and electronic influences. The tracks have received major international radio support, with Don’t Listen also featured on the FC26 soundtrack.

Over the past two years, corto.alto has played more than 150 shows worldwide, including Glastonbury, We Out Here, Montreux and North Sea Jazz, as well as a sold-out 2,000-capacity show at Glasgow’s Barrowland Ballroom.

Supported by names such as Gilles Peterson, Jamie Cullum and BBC Radio 6 Music, he represents a new generation of artists blurring the lines between jazz, beats and club culture.
excerpt: The Scottish composer, producer and multi-instrumentalist Liam Shortall, aka corto.alto, has emerged as one of the most exciting voices on the new European jazz scene – catch him live at Nefertiti on October 17.

featuredmedia.alt_text: Liam Shortall

title: Jasper Høiby’s 3Elements (DK)
content:
Høiby is best known as the founder of the influential group Phronesis, which helped redefine the modern piano trio format since its formation in 2005.

Now presenting Conversations of Hope, the trio’s third release on Edition Records, the music moves with intensity and precision. With Naíma Acuña on drums and Xavi Torres on piano, the trio blends strong melodic ideas, shifting time signatures, and a sharp sense of space and dynamics. Acuña’s driving rhythmic clarity and Torres’ harmonically rich piano work lock tightly into Høiby’s bass-led compositions, resulting in music that feels urgent, physical and constantly in motion.

Featuring: Jasper Høiby (bass), Xavi Torres (piano), Naíma Acuña (drums).
excerpt: Jasper Høiby’s 3Elements is a piano trio led by one of contemporary jazz’s most respected bassists and composers.

featuredmedia.alt_text: Jasper Høiby

title: Kevin Bridges-Here if you need me
content:
Kevin is one of the sharpest and most original voices in stand-up comedy today! And he’s bringing his brand-new show to Gothenburg Concert Hall.

He’s been featured on Netflix, sold out the Beacon Theatre in New York, and has more than two million fans worldwide.

Performed in English.
excerpt: Warm, fearless, brilliant, funny, alive.

featuredmedia.alt_text: stand up artist kevin bridges

title: Ein deutsches Requiem
content:
Take the opportunity to experience the new Swedish star soprano Christina Nilsson in Johannes Brahms’s masterpiece Ein deutsches Requiem. Together with baritone soloist Christoph Pohl, the Gothenburg Symphony Orchestra and the Gothenburg Symphony Chorus, conductor Marie Jacquot leads us to a place that reminds us of what Christmas may be most deeply about: hope, humanity and togetherness.

It took nearly ten years for Johannes Brahms to complete A German Requiem. The work was finished in 1868, three years after the death of his mother. It was also his major breakthrough. This is not a typical religious funeral mass for the dead. Rather, Brahms presents a comforting perspective for the living.

Christina Nilsson’s breakthrough came with her performance as Aida at the Royal Swedish Opera in 2018. Since then, she has sung at the world’s major opera houses. Last year she was appointed as court singer. And for the second time this year, we get to hear popular French conductor Marie Jacquot, chief conductor of the Royal Danish Theatre in Copenhagen. Together, they create a ceremonial and consoling evening for the Christmas season.

Come closer

Have a seat in the Great Hall an hour before the concert and let the introduction open the door to the stories behind the works, facts about the composers and personal reflections. The introduction is included in your ticket, lasts about 30 minutes and has free seating in the hall.
excerpt: Brahms’s magnificent choral work reminds us of what Christmas may be most deeply about: hope, humanity and togetherness.

featuredmedia.alt_text: Christina Nilsson

title: Orphei Drängar sing Sibelius
content:
Jean Sibelius’ breakthrough as a composer came with the symphonic suite Kullervo. He was inspired by the Finnish national epic, the Kalevala, and ancient songs from Karelia. The evening features the magnificent male choir Orphei Drängar, and Santtu-Matias Rouvali presents Sibelius’ epic stories with expertise.

The suite about the life and death of the tragic figure Kullervo is a diamond in the rough among Sibelius’ numerous compositions. Its reception was enthusiastic, but Sibelius withdrew it. He felt the suite was musically immature, and it was not performed again until after his death in 1957.

It is a true experience to hear Uppsala’s renowned men’s choir Orphei Drängar, with 80 members. Popular conductor Santtu-Matias Rouvali, chief conductor of the orchestra for many years, returns to Gothenburg at last with his marvellous feel for Sibelius’ music. He and the orchestra have received acclaim for their recordings of Sibelius’ complete seven symphonies.
excerpt: Hear the fateful Kullervo – music filled with power, choral sounds and mystery. The magnificent male choir Orphei Drängar sing, and Santtu-Matias Rouvali leads the Gothenburg Symphony Orchestra in Sibelius’ spectacular symphonic poem.

featuredmedia.alt_text: Santtu-Matias Rouvali conducts the Gothenburg Symphony Orchestra in Sibelius's powerful tondikt.

title: Electric guitar through fire & water
content:
Experience the unusual presentation of a classical concert for orchestra and electric guitar. As soloist, we hear guitar virtuoso Magnus Andersson. Composer Ming Tsao is from the US and has also been active in Gothenburg. His music dissolves the symphonic form, allowing sounds to transport the audience to a free space in which they can let their thoughts wander.

Then we travel to a galaxy far, far away in Williams’ wonderful film score from Star Wars! Take the opportunity to experience the space journey with a live orchestra in the Great Hall. The powerful and solemn atmosphere is built up by American Aaron Copland’s classic Fanfare for the Common Man.

After the intermission, we are cast into the famous suite from The Firebird. Composer Igor Stravinsky had just taken the western world by storm when, in 1910, he composed the first of several legendary ballets. Here, he combines his orchestral sorcery with Russian folk songs and fairy tales. The result is a dazzling atmosphere in the story of the evil Koschei and the captive princesses, who are finally freed by the mesmerising Firebird. Prepare for one of the great finales of music history.

Come closer

Have a seat in the Great Hall an hour before the concert and let the introduction open the door to the stories behind the works, facts about the composers and personal reflections. The introduction is included in your ticket, lasts about 30 minutes and has free seating in the hall.
excerpt: A world premiere by composer Ming Tsao that gives off sparks! The electric guitar is in focus, backed by the entire Gothenburg Symphony. Conductor Brad Lubman also hands us Stravinsky’s famous suite from The Firebird and music from Star Wars.

featuredmedia.alt_text: Conductor Brad Lubman

title: Family Concert: Pippi Longstocking at the Concert Hall
content:
Anything can happen when Astrid Lindgren’s Pippi Longstocking visits the Gothenburg Symphony Orchestra! Pippi meets a real conductor and goes on a scavenger hunt among all the instruments. And can she get an entire orchestra to fall asleep?

Of course, police officers Kling and Klang do their best to put a stop to Pippi’s mischief.
excerpt: It’s time for Astrid Lindgren’s Pippi Longstocking to visit the Gothenburg Symphony Orchestra! Pippi meets a real conductor and goes on a scavenger hunt among all the instruments. And can she get an entire orchestra to fall asleep? From age 6.
