title: Big feelings from Schumann & Beach
content:
As a major star in the 19th century, pianist Clara Schumann toured Europe. As a married woman, she had to abandon her own composition practice, but she remained a highly respected musician and ambassador for her husband Robert Schumann’s music. They were considered the most exciting couple in music at the time.

Robert Schumann composed his String Quartet No. 3 during a few intense weeks of summer, when he and Clara had been married for two years. The quartet is rhythmic and full of long, romantic melodies.

American composer and pianist Amy Beach paints her Piano Quintet with dramatic brush strokes. She embarked upon her professional path as a pianist already as a teenager. Her concerts were put on hold when she was married, but she was famous in the US and Europe in her own lifetime. The Piano Quintet in F-Sharp Minor premiered in Boston with Beach herself on piano 118 years ago.
excerpt: With a light and careful approach, musicians from the Gothenburg Symphony present an emotional chamber music concert. Music from two female pioneers becomes an intimate conversation between the piano and strings.

featuredmedia.alt_text: Juan Zurutuza by the piano

title: Mozart with Martin Fröst
content:
Swedish clarinet star Martin Fröst continues to captivate audiences as both a soloist and conductor. He is soloist in the beloved Clarinet Concerto, one of Mozart’s most beautiful works – and the one that made Fröst world-famous. There won’t be a dry eye in the house during the delicate adagio. Fröst has interpreted this work no fewer than three times in recordings, and says there is no definitive version.

“Each performance of a work is its own expression, contains its own truth … I have changed, both as an artist and as a person. And we change as listeners.”, Fröst says.

Before Martin Fröst takes the stage, the concert kicks off with a sugar rush. Swedish composer Tebogo Monnakgotla has written the humorous piece Sugar High, inspired by sugar rushes at children’s parties.

To conclude, we settle into a space of love and longing with Brahms’ Symphony No. 2. The orchestra is led by German conductor Cornelius Meister in this long-awaited return to Gothenburg.

Come closer

Have a seat in the Great Hall an hour before the concert and let the introduction open the door to the stories behind the works, facts about the composers and personal reflections. The introduction is included in your ticket, lasts about 30 minutes and has free seating in the hall.
excerpt: Join in for mischief and play! Clarinet star Martin Fröst and the Gothenburg Symphony Orchestra play Mozart’s Clarinet Concerto, a piece in constant motion. We promise a sugar rush and pounding hearts.

featuredmedia.alt_text: Clarinetist Martin Fröst

title: Bach Jazz
content:
J.S. Bach is the genius behind Air, Mass in B Minor, St. John Passion and many other masterpieces. Preludes, partitas, sarabandes – there are many works and even more interpretations. Emil Carlsson Rinstad, bass player Magnus Bergström, and drummer Ola Winkler have mastered the material completely.

The music magazine Lira referred to their debut album as the “chamber jazz of the year.” “Suddenly Bach sounds like a Nordic composer and his fugues like folk songs,” added Swedish newspaper DN. And echoes of Jan Johansson’s sound are as present as the immediately recognizable notes of Bach.

The careful improvisations are more of an addition to or comment on Bach than full-scale reconstructions. Utterly open and warm, thoughtful and exploratory, time and again, they present new aspects of Bach’s infinite starry sky.
excerpt: Hear compelling and swinging interpretations of masterpieces composed by J.S. Bach. Gothenburg-based trio Bach Jazz have touched audiences’ hearts with this new take on elegant Baroque music.

featuredmedia.alt_text: Gothenburg Trio Bach Jazz

title: Pekka Kuusisto in Sibelius Violin Concert
content:
Principal Guest Conductor Pekka Kuusisto brings fellow countryman Sibelius’ beloved Violin Concerto, which he has played throughout his career. This time, he leads the orchestra himself, with violin in hand.

Jean Sibelius was an outstanding violinist, but never really broke through as a virtuoso. The Violin Concerto in D Minor (1905) can be seen as a tribute to the instrument and its various expressions, with powerful intensity and Nordic melancholy. In Pekka Kuusisto’s interpretation, the concerto is continuously fresh and new.

“There is reason to see the concert as less of a heroic tale, and more as something channeled from the earth, or from the ancestors – as a kind of shamanistic event.”
Pekka Kuusisto

The evening begins with Andrea Tarrodi’s Birds of Paradise, in which the orchestra vibrates with the forces of nature and birdsong. To conclude, Kuusisto exchanges his violin for the conductor’s baton again to lead the Gothenburg Symphony in Tchaikovsky’s emotionally charged Symphony No. 5.

The concert is also performed on the Gothenburg Symphony’s tour to Amsterdam and Dublin.

Come closer

Have a seat in the Great Hall an hour before the concert and let the introduction open the door to the stories behind the works, facts about the composers and personal reflections. The introduction is included in your ticket, lasts about 30 minutes and has free seating in the hall.
excerpt: Explosiveness, tempo and rest as Pekka Kuusisto plays and conducts Sibelius’ Violin Concerto with the Gothenburg Symphony Orchestra. In Kuusisto’s hands, the music is born anew.

featuredmedia.alt_text: Pekka Kuusisto

title: Shimmering Horn Concerto by Helen Grime
content:
Scottish composer Helen Grime aims to create a new sound world that is unique to each piece. She is drawn to long, expressive lines and rich harmonies. Grime composed this horn concerto specifically for the Gothenburg Symphony Orchestra’s Alec Frank-Gemmill, one of Europe’s leading soloists on his instrument, who always adds a touch of shimmer and sensuality to the music.

Helen Grime’s work was most recently performed in Gothenburg in 2024, when her Trumpet Concerto, night-sky-blue, was played by Håkan Hardenberger.

Conductor Eun Sun Kim, from South Korea, is chief conductor of the San Francisco Opera. She expertly guides the Gothenburg Symphony through Korngold’s only completed symphony, composed in 1952. Adventurous melodies and sizzling love themes can be heard here, as in the film score for which Korngold became so famous.

Come closer

Have a seat in the Great Hall an hour before the concert and let the introduction open the door to the stories behind the works, facts about the composers and personal reflections. The introduction is included in your ticket, lasts about 30 minutes and has free seating in the hall.
excerpt: High intensity and cinematic tones prevail as Alec Frank-Gemmill plays a fresh horn concerto by Helen Grime, together with the Gothenburg Symphony Orchestra. Korngold’s symphony is gentle and moving under the baton of Eun Sun Kim.

featuredmedia.alt_text: Helen Grime

title: Ice cold with Terje Isungset Ice Quartet
content:
Terje Isungset has performed in Stenhammarsalen  several times with shimmering improvisations as the drummer in folk music ensemble Group. Now he returns with water in solid form.

Since 1999, when Isungset composed music under a frozen waterfall in Lillehammer, he has explored the extraordinary sound potential of ice. This has resulted in several albums of ice music and an annual Ice Music Festival.

Isungset’s discovery of the music of ice resulted from a moment of pure inspiration: “I was recording the sound of the waterfall when I was just struck by the ice. It was so beautiful. It was like being in love.”

With instruments such as an ice harp, ice horn, iceophone and ice bass alongside more traditional instruments and songs, the quartet freely explores an evocative and dynamic style. The unpredictability of the instruments results in a unique concert every time: bubbling sounds, cool overtones and rhythms that bear traces of the landscape in which melting water once froze and became ice.
excerpt: What happens when music literally melts? Terje Isungset and his Ice Quartet play instruments sculpted from naturally frozen ice from Norwegian lakes. Experience sounds and tones that only exist here and now.

featuredmedia.alt_text: Terje Isungse

title: Icona Pop
content:
Caroline Hjelt and Aino Jawo, globally known as the duo Icona Pop, are back with new music and a Nordic tour. This Friday sees the release of “Butterfly Feelings”, the third single from their upcoming album RITUAL, set for release in August. They will then take the new material on the road, with a series of Nordic dates in October and November.

The first half of 2026 has marked a strong comeback for Icona Pop. So far, the duo have released two acclaimed singles from the forthcoming album: the title track “Ritual” and the recent “Dance to This”. The new music blends Icona Pop’s signature club sound with themes of friendship, motherhood, healing and self‑discovery – all without losing the explosive energy that has made them one of Sweden’s biggest pop exports.

On May 13, Icona Pop kicked off the summer concert season with a sold‑out show at Trädgården in Stockholm. In early November, they will return to their hometown. Caroline and Aino went from being club kids in Stockholm to dominating clubs, arenas and festivals worldwide. Their major breakthrough came in 2012 with the “Billions Club”‑certified hit “I Love It” featuring Charli XCX – a track that has become an anthem for a whole generation.
excerpt: Icona Pop celebrate their new album with a Nordic tour.

featuredmedia.alt_text: Icona Pop

title: Old town Haga walking tour
content:
Known for its cobbled streets, hidden courtyards, and well-preserved wooden houses, Haga offers a unique glimpse into the city’s past and present.

During the tour, you’ll learn about Gothenburg’s fascinating history, working-class heritage, distinctive architecture, and transformation into one of Scandinavia’s most creative and vibrant cities.

Along the way, your guide will share stories about Swedish culture, local traditions, and everyday life while pointing out details and places often missed by visitors.

Duration: 90 minutes.

Please note that this tour is not accessible for wheelchair users.
excerpt: Discover Haga, one of Gothenburg’s most charming and historic neighbourhoods.

featuredmedia.alt_text: Visitors stroll along Haga’s charming pedestrian street, lined with historic buildings, cafés and shops in Gothenburg.

title: Pumpkin Bowl 2026
content:
An international meeting place in Gothenburg

Pumpkin Bowl is one of Europe’s most international flag football tournaments and takes place annually in Prioritet Serneke Arena in Gothenburg during the Halloween weekend. The event brings together players, teams, and supporters from Sweden, Europe, and beyond for a weekend filled with sport, community, and unforgettable experiences.

Previous editions have welcomed teams from both Europe and South America, and the ambition for 2026 is to attract participants from Africa and North America as well. Through its international reach, Pumpkin Bowl continues to strengthen Gothenburg’s position as a destination for sports tourism and global events.

On the road to LA 2028

Flag football is one of the fastest-growing team sports in the world and will make its Olympic debut at the Los Angeles 2028 Olympic Games. Pumpkin Bowl offers a unique opportunity to experience the sport up close, featuring everyone from rising young talent to established elite players from multiple countries.

Bigger than ever

For the 2026 edition, Pumpkin Bowl has the capacity to host up to 60 teams, making it one of the largest flag football events in Europe. Teams compete across multiple divisions and age categories, creating an inclusive environment for youth athletes, recreational players, and elite competitors alike.

Visitors can look forward to exciting games, an international atmosphere, and a welcoming environment for players, families, and spectators. Free admission.
excerpt: Pumpkin Bowl brings together teams from Europe and around the world for a unique weekend of flag football, community, and international competition. Experience one of Europe’s most exciting events for the world’s fastest-growing Olympic team sport.

featuredmedia.alt_text: A flag football player in a purple uniform sprints across the field with the ball secured in one hand, eyes focused downfield as defenders close in pursuit behind her. The action captures a decisive breakaway moment, showcasing speed, agility, and determination during a competitive game.

title: Classical After Work: La voix humaine
content:
Join Gothenburg’s most classical after-work event! The doors open at 16:00 pm to Gothenburg Concert Hall for an afternoon of socialising, music and new friends. Gather your friends, enjoy something from the bar, and settle in to the atmosphere before this evening’s After Work concert in the Great Hall at 18:00 pm (approximately one hour long).

Tonight, you get to experience international star Barbara Hannigan as soprano and conductor in Poulenc’s renowned one-act opera, together with the Gothenburg Symphony Orchestra. It is a gripping performance about the last conversation on the phone between two lovers.

When the last note has rung out, the evening goes on in the foyer bars until 21:00. Live music continues, discussions deepen and twilight arrives at Götaplatsen.
excerpt: Stop by after work for music, mingling and drinks from the bar. The Gothenburg Symphony Orchestra and Barbara Hannigan present the gripping one-act opera about the last conversation between two lovers.

featuredmedia.alt_text: Barbara Hannigan

title: Organ Concert: Anna von Hausswolff in Depth
content:
Gothenburg musician Anna von Hausswolff has taken the music world by storm with her avant-garde pop. Her latest album, Iconoclasts, was celebrated as one of the best albums of 2025.

She is now presenting her organ music in an instrumental concert. Here, she performs music from her albums All Thoughts Fly and The Lower Depths – the former of which was inspired by the Italian sculpture park Sacro Bosco, and recorded on the Baroque organ in Örgryte New Church. The latter was written for the Royal Dramatic Theatre show Natthärbärget (“The Lower Depths”).

The arrangements are by Anna von Hausswolff, Filip Leyman and avant-garde saxophone player Otis Sandsjö. With three organists and three woodwinds, as well as sound processing and electronics, the pieces are presented in a surround system. Together with the 9,000 vibrating pipes of the Concert Hall organ, this will be an experience beyond the ordinary with a world-class artist.

“Music that is solemn, echo-laden, heavy on the drone of her beloved pipe organ and fully deserving of the adjective gothic.” – The Guardian
excerpt: Internationally acclaimed Anna von Hausswolff takes over the Concert Hall’s large organ in a unique solo programme. Hear works from the theatre and stage for organ, woodwinds and electronic instruments.

featuredmedia.alt_text: An organ on the stage.

title: To the Light with Mendelssohn and Fauré
content:
A concert characterised by meditative prayer and romantic drama. As a peaceful end point, we hear Fauré’s reassuring and beloved Requiem – a work that surrounds the listener with warmth, light and inner peace.

Lili Boulanger called her work “Old Buddhist Prayer”, an early 20th-century work inspired by the Buddhist text tradition. It is infused with contemplation and mystery, and time and space seem to pause. This is followed by Franz Schreker’s Chamber Symphony, which represents late-Romantic modernism, with dense orchestral movements and a richly colourful sound.
Mendelssohn’s concert overture is depicting the ocean’s mirror-smooth stillness and sudden movement. It is inspired by two poems by Goethe. The concert concludes with Fauré’s Requiem, one of music history’s most heartfelt requiems – known for its light and reassuring sound, rather than doomsday rhetoric.

Step inside, join the community and relax with the orchestra, choir and soloists.

title: No limits with Gageego!
content:
The ensemble Gageego! are on a continuous journey of discovery through contemporary music. Here, they explore science and art in works by composers including Britta Byström, Jesper Nordin and Anna Thorvaldsdottir.

Multi-award-winning composer Britta Byström has created music for poet Inger Christensen’s poetry collection Alphabet. She was deeply moved by the poems, which follow the Fibonacci sequence – the number of rows grows longer and longer, following a predetermined rate of increase. Similarly, the movements of Byström’s composition become longer and longer. Byström was inspired by how the details of beauty in nature become a protective spell against all threats.

Science and art are similarly merged by Anna Thorvaldsdottir in her Entropic Arrows, where the music is an effort to reflect the physical world. Jesper Nordin’s piece Surfaces Scintillantes is something of the opposite. What we hear on the surface, he explains, is simply the basic material. He composed the piece using a digital drawing board.
excerpt: The curious ensemble Gageego! take us on a winding journey through poetry and science. Discover new music by Britta Byström, Jesper Nordin and Anna Thorvaldsdottir that breaks down all barriers.

title: Rumours of Fleetwood Mac
content:
Rumours of Fleetwood Mac, personally endorsed and supported by Fleetwood Mac founder Mick Fleetwood, is widely regarded as the ultimate tribute to one of the most iconic bands in rock history.

As the band hits the road in 2027, one of popular culture’s most influential albums takes centre stage. It has been 50 years since the release of Rumours, the landmark album that gave the world timeless classics such as “Go Your Own Way,” “Dreams,” “The Chain,” and “Don’t Stop.” The album has shaped generations of music lovers and continues to be discovered by millions of new listeners today.

During this special anniversary concert, audiences will be taken on a journey through Fleetwood Mac’s legendary catalogue, performed with the precision, musicianship, and passion that have made Rumours of Fleetwood Mac a global audience favourite. With deep respect for the original material and a unique stage production, the band successfully recreates the magic and extraordinary energy of Fleetwood Mac at the height of their success.

Whether you have been a fan since 1977 or have only recently discovered the music through streaming services and social media, an unforgettable live experience filled with nostalgia and emotion awaits.

Information from the organizer

Age limit: 13+.

Strobe lighting and flashing light effects will be used.

title: Spring Concert with Heyward & Hardenberger
content:
Jonathon Heyward, the young music director of the Baltimore Symphony Orchestra, takes us on a dramatic journey with spring right around the corner. Shostakovich’s Symphony No. 7 is called the Leningrad Symphony, and it vibrates with the pain from the occupation during World War II. The symphony is a moving experience requiring the collected resources of the entire orchestra.

But before that we hear world star Håkan Hardenberger, called in the press an “undisputed master” of the trumpet, and mentioned in the same breath as Louis Armstrong, Miles Davis and Dizzy Gillespie. Here he performs a rare trumpet concerto by Bernd Alois Zimmerman with influences from the big bands of the 1950s. The orchestra is also expanded with a jazz band and Hammond organ.

Zimmerman worked his whole life to integrate free improvisation into orchestral music. The trumpet concerto Nobody knows de trouble I see from 1954 is a key work, and fundamentally a criticism of racial hatred and the mechanisms that were behind the Second World War.

Conductor Jonathon Heyward is a star in the making. And he has an expressed mission: to play classical music that everyone can enjoy. He is the youngest music director of a large US symphony orchestra, the Baltimore Symphony Orchestra, and a frequent guest conductor with Europe’s leading symphony orchestras.

title: Classical After Work: Pettersson’s 7th
content:

title: Royal Stockholm Philharmonic Orchestra & Bruce Liu
content:
Canadian pianist Bruce Liu won the international Chopin Competition in 2021. Tonight, Rachmaninoff’s challenging variations on Paganini’s well-known theme are on the menu. Tempo and drama are guaranteed!

Niccolò Paganini was an unparalleled violinist and superstar whom everyone wanted to hear. Numerous composers have been inspired by the short pieces of his 24 Caprices. Sergei Rachmaninoff’s romantic variations on Paganini’s theme push the boundaries and are based on a close collaboration with the orchestra.

As an introduction, we hear Swedish Benjamin Staern’s dazzling orchestral work Jubilate from 2009. It contains all the celebration, drama and victory of a football stadium.

The evening also concludes with drama in Carl Nielsen’s Symphony No. 2.  “The Four Temperaments” present an entire range of the human psyche.

title: Karin Hammar Fab 4
content:
Norwegian trumpet player Hildegunn Øiseth works worldwide and is able to evoke a swinging sound from an ancient bockhorn. She has collaborated with percussionist Marilyn Mazur, Radiojazzgruppen and the Bohuslän Big Band when not leading her own quartet.

Karin Hammar is one of Sweden’s top trombone players, known from numerous TV shows and her own ensembles Sliding Hammers and Karin Hammar Good Vibe. Here, she is at the helm of the Fab 4 with guitarist Andreas Hourdakis, bass player Pär-Ola Landin and drummer Fredrik Rundqvist.

In an interview with magazine Orkester Journalen, Karin Hammar said: “The best thing about jazz is that feeling of freedom – you can just about play however you want.” In other words, an evening with Karin Hammar Fab 4 and Hildegunn Øiseth is an evening where anything can happen.
excerpt: Anything can happen when trombone player Karin Hammar and her Fab 4 take the stage. In this combo with acclaimed trumpet player Hildegunn Øiseth, she delivers deeply swinging and exploratory jazz that is full of surprises.

title: Symfonic Fairy Tales
content:
In the incredibly popular symphonic suite Scheherazade, Nikolai Rimsky-Korsakov takes us into the tales of One Thousand and One Nights. The composer’s ability to colour his music was impressive, and the work is full of scenic melodies. Soloists and orchestra really get to shine here, led by Spanish conductor Jaime Martín.

The folktale collection One Thousand and One Nights can be traced all the way back to the ninth century. In the story, Scheherazade begins a new tale each night, and manages to get the king so eager to hear the end that he abandons his cruel and evil killing plan.

We also get to hear a brand new piece of Swedish music: a vivid cello concerto. Award-winning composer Mats Larsson Gothe, who also participated in the concert project Nordic – A Fragile Hope, composed the concerto for his friend, cellist Torleif Thedéen, who is the soloist for the evening. Delicate, floating melodies and grand drama can all be heard here. The concerto makes use of all the emotional material a cello is capable of: longing and dreams, rage and resignation.

title: The Phantom in the Organ and on Screen
content:
Take this chance to experience a silent film as it was presented one hundred years ago. At that time, live music created tension and highlighted the emotions on screen.

A phantom haunts the Paris Opera House. It pursues the singers and takes over their senses. Visitors die in the salon under mysterious circumstances. The Phantom of the Opera from 1925 is based on a novel with the same name by Gaston Leroux, and is considered one of the major horror classics. In 1986, the story became a hit musical with music by Andrew Lloyd Webber.

British organist David Briggs is a well-known improviser and composer. He is now guest-performing in Gothenburg for the first time, offering a truly scary cinematic adventure with the help of the Concert Hall organ.

Introduction to the concert

Arrive in the Main Hall an hour before the concert and ease into what you’re about to experience. Here, you’ll learn more about the music, the organ, and the film.

The introduction is included in your ticket, lasts approximately 30 minutes, and offers open seating. Take a seat wherever you like—and let the concert begin right here.
excerpt: Experience silent film with live music! David Briggs improvises on the large Concert Hall organ to the 1925 classic horror film, The Phantom of the Opera. Expect cold shivers and a deadly thirst for love.

title: Sibelius Symphony No. 2 with Sallinen
content:
Follow along on a journey through three eras with Finland’s foremost composers. This is the Swedish premiere of a new organ concerto composed by Sebastian Fagerlund, one of Europe’s most prominent composers of his generation. The soloist is the charismatic Iveta Apkalna, who is at the forefront of discovering and presenting new music for organ.

But we begin with music from the 1920s, Moonlight on Jupiter, with the subtitle “Fantastic tone poem for orchestra”. Composer Väinö Raitio was a leading figure of Finnish modernism and a bit of a rebel. Moonlight became a theme for the Finnish fight for freedom, as did Sibelius’ Symphony No. 2 – even if Sibelius himself asserted that his music was just music and nothing more. The conductor is the talented young Kristian Sallinen.

Sebastian Fagerlund is from Pargas and composes music for orchestras and conductors around the world, with a strong sense of the large format and the instruments’ virtuosity.

title: Music from the salons of Paris
content:
A chamber orchestra from the Gothenburg Symphony Orchestra presents a beautiful blend of music with a fragrance of La Belle Époque. Enjoy nostalgic music, such as delights from Wagner’s Tristan und Isolde, and Couperin’s lovely piece for harpsichord, Les Barricades Mystérieuses. Sounds from the new twentieth century are also heard, such as Vaughan Williams’ Piano Quintet, and Fauré’s Cello Sonata No. 1, transcribed here for double bass.

The orchestra is led by the two concertmasters Sara Trobäck and Justyna Jara.

Paris during La Belle Époque was an idyllic meeting place for composers, poets and writers. After long and difficult wars, France entered an era of peace from the late nineteenth century until World War I broke out in 1914. It was a light-hearted time characterised by financial growth and faith in the future. People enjoyed the good in life.

France’s own Gabriel Fauré was often on the programme in French salons. Here, we hear a bittersweet piece by Fauré from 1917, in which the ageing composer looks back in search of lost time.
excerpt: Follow along to La Belle Époque – the good life in Paris around the turn of the 19th century. Hear music from the lovely salons and dream away of this bygone era, with musicians from the Gothenburg Symphony Orchestra.

title: Eagles of Death Metal
content:
Eagles of Death Metal are an American rock band from Palm Desert, California, founded in 1998 by Jesse Hughes and Joshua Homme. Over the years, the band has featured a wide range of musicians both in the studio and on stage. The current touring line‑up consists of frontman Hughes, Leah Bluestein (drums), Scott Shiflett (guitar) and Dustin Douglas (bass).

Despite the name, Eagles of Death Metal are not a death metal band – the name is intended as a joke. With a sound described as “bluegrass slide guitar mixed with stripper drum beats and Canned Heat vocals”, and a frontman in Hughes known for his flamboyant stage antics and strong audience connection, their live shows are truly something to experience.

EODM have released four studio albums to date — Peace Love Death Metal, Death by Sexy, Heart On and Zipper Down — and have toured extensively around the world over the past two decades. A brand‑new studio album is currently in the works and soon set to be released.

title: Daniel Sloss: Bitter
content:
Don’t miss your chance to catch one of the biggest global names in live stand-up, as Scotland’s international comedy superstar Daniel Sloss unleashes his brilliant and devastatingly hilarious brand-new show “BITTER”.

Daniel’s massive live tours span 55 countries (so far)including selling out 9 New York off-Broadway theatre seasons. He has been performing stand-up for more than half of his lifetime and has, in the process, broken multiple box office records to become one of the top ticket-selling comedians on the planet. BITTER is his 13th solo show.

His comedy specials include “Jigsaw” and “DARK” on Netflix, “X” on HBO as well as “SOCIO”, “HUBRIS”, “X” and ”CAN’T” now streaming on DanielSloss.com.

title: Spiritual Sounds from Morocco
content:
When Majid Bekkas takes the stage, Moroccan tradition meets the deeply emotional expression of the blues. He is one of North Africa’s most luminous musical voices and a master of the guembri – the three-string instrument with a vibrating sound.

Gnawa music has origins in the African diaspora and spiritual ceremonies. It carries stories of loss, forgiveness and survival – themes that are also at the heart of the blues. Majid Bekkas ties these worlds together through improvisation, groove and a voice that moves freely between song, prayer and storytelling.

Majid Bekkas’ international breakthrough came with Daymallah, the opening track to the popular, award-winning compilation album Desert Blues 2 (2001).

Alongside his fellow musicians, he creates an evocative sound in which the call and response, recurring riffs and free solos of the blues are woven together with North African rhythms and melodies. The music slowly builds up in intensity, inspiring deep listening and – if you are open to it – a trance-like state.
excerpt: Majid Bekkas unites Moroccan tradition with the deeply emotional expression of the blues. Hear one of North Africa’s most luminous musical voices and master of the guembri – the warmly vibrating three-string instrument.

title: Mahler Symphony No. 5
content:
Mahler’s Symphony No. 5 vibrates with horror and harmony in a frightful blend, from the famous trumpet fanfare of the opening to the swaying Viennese waltz. There is also the famous adagietto’s gorgeous tapestry of strings, floating between dream and wakefulness. Mahler composed it as a love letter to his Alma.

But first, we hear newly composed music from acclaimed Finnish composer Sauli Zinovjev. His Wiegenlied (lullaby) for Orchestra premiered in Oslo in 2020 and is a joint commission of the Gothenburg Symphony Orchestra. Conducting tonight is Pierre Bleuse, popular principal conductor of the Odense Symphony Orchestra.

Debussy’s beloved Prelude begins the concert. This dreamy depiction of a resting faun contains exciting harmonies that revolutionised music in their time.

title: Aaron Parks Trio
content:
Aaron Parks was the multi-talented prodigy who chose music over maths and computer science. Today, he is considered one of the most influential pianists of modern jazz, a visionary who makes “jazz for the new century.”

Aaron Parks caught the attention of major names early on; they all heard something unique. On his own, he has continued to refine his intuitive ability to transcend musical genres. His distinctive sound combines electronica and hip hop, hints of early Keith Jarrett and creative rock band Radiohead. Just as naturally, bebop is paired with minimalism or Eastern loops – and all of it is infused with traces of the airy sound that is the signature of record label ECM.

The Aaron Parks Trio includes Swedish drummer Cornelia Nilsson, who has already played with legends like Ron Carter and Kenny Barron. With drumming that is both expressive and technically brilliant, she is a natural partner.
excerpt: Experience American visionary Aaron Parks, one of the most influential pianists of modern jazz. He makes jazz for our time, combining everything from hip hop to rock and bebop. Performing this evening with Cornelia Nilsson on drums.

title: Barber cello concerto
content:
This is Chinese-Australian Qin’s first performance in Sweden. The music ranges from Samuel Barber’s emotional Cello Concerto to Sergei Rachmaninoff’s lyrically expansive Symphony No. 2, all under the baton of conductor Holly Hyun Choe in a welcome return.

Samuel Barber’s Cello Concerto from 1945 is an expressive work, characterised by powerful melodies and dramatic contrasts. The soloist offers virtuosic intensity in the outer movements, and lyrical introspection in the dreamy second movement.  It is no wonder that this is among the most beloved cello concertos. Cellist Li-Wei Qin was born in Shanghai and has a rich career behind him, in which he has performed with all of the major orchestras.

Symphony number 2 in E Minor, is one of Rachmaninoff’s most beloved and popular works, composed between 1906–1907 after a period of depression. It is known for its grand, romantic expressiveness, especially in the famous third adagio movement, as well as the triumphant finale.

Holly Hyun Choe, who leads the Norwegian Radio Orchestra, lets the Gothenburg Symphony’s entire register find expression in this late-Romantic work.

title: Early summer tango
content:
The little bandoneon accordion is the heart of tango, and it is often in the foreground of Astor Piazzolla’s music. It is played here by a true master: Henrik Sandås. Violinist Emirzeth Henríquez leads a quartet from the Gothenburg Symphony Orchestra.
The evening is devoted to tango, the music that emerged among immigrants in Buenos Aires and the Port of Montevideo, which had roots in Europe, Africa and Cuba. The immeasurably popular Astor Piazzolla transformed elegantly dancing tango music, taking it from tired bars to the concert music of tango nuevo.

Unforgettable pieces of music include Libertango, Oblivion and La Muerte del Angel: melancholy, mournful, emotional. Like many others, Piazzolla was inspired by the seasons, and this evening we hear two of his four pieces.

Henrik Sandås, a musician as likely to play Baroque as jazz and symphonic tango nuevo, plays bandoneon and arranged the music.

The string quartet from the Gothenburg Symphony Orchestra includes, in addition to violinist Emirzeth Henríquez, Hanna Eliasson, violin; Tuula Fleivik Nurmo, viola; and Petra Lundin, cello.
excerpt: An evening dedicated to tango and Astor Piazzolla’s sensual music. With a string quartet and bandoneon, we hear beloved pieces from the Argentine master’s rich repertoire.

title: Chaplin Songs
content:
The Great Dictator (1940) was Chaplin’s first sound film and his response to an era characterised by Nazism and fascism. In the final scene, he gives a passionate speech for peace in which he urges the soldiers to stop the war: “Let us fight to free the world – to do away with national barriers – to do away with greed, with hate and intolerance.”

These words were the starting point for Swedish composer Daniel Nelson’s Chaplin Songs – a musical reflection of both the speech and the relevance of the entire film:

“In a time when the foundations of democracy are threatened both by individual people and by entire ideologies, Chaplin Songs is my way of re-telling the message to which Chaplin gave voice in the film’s speech: if we do not preserve democracy, we are all doomed,” says Nelson.

As soprano soloist, we hear the acclaimed Camilla Tilling, who also gave the premiere performance in 2022 of this award-winning work.

Hugo Alfvén’s Symphony No. 3 has its own Gothenburg-based history, as it premiered in this city in 1906, led by Alfvén himself. Nordic romance and continental joie de vivre are united here. He dedicated the work to his wife, Marie Kröyer.

title: On the Road with Byström & Beethoven
content:
With rich and playful sounds, surprising turns and impressionistic elements, composer Britta Byström creates an imaginative musical journey. The music is infused with a thirst for discovery in the spirit of Jules Verne. Byström’s large-scale work for orchestra, Voyages Extraordinaires, first premiered in 2023 by the Gothenburg Symphony Orchestra and will now be taken to Stockholm for a guest performance.

Beethoven’s Symphony No. 7 was composed in 1811–1812 and is characterised by its rhythmic energy, often described as his most dance-like work. The focus here is on movement and pulse, which led Wagner to refer to the symphony as the “apotheosis of the dance” (becoming god-like).

The symphony is an example of Ludwig van Beethoven’s ability to combine dramatic intensity with luminous melodies. This is an occasion to celebrate the 200-year anniversary of Beethoven, especially through the famous melody of the second movement, which has been used in both songs and movie soundtracks.

Pekka Kuusisto is Principal Guest Conductor at Gothenburg Symphony, celebrated for his artistic freedom and creative attitude towards the classical repertoire.

Come closer

Have a seat in the Great Hall an hour before the concert and let the introduction open the door to the stories behind the works, facts about the composers and personal reflections. The introduction is included in your ticket, lasts about 30 minutes and has free seating in the hall.
excerpt: Gothenburg Symphony Orchestra and conductor Pekka Kuusisto conclude the season with power and energy. We hear Britta Byström’s colourful orchestral adventure and celebrate Beethoven’s anniversary with the life-affirming Symphony No. 7.

title: Buika- World tour 2026
content:
With her gently veiled voice, steeped in the heart’s longing, sorrow, and melancholy, this acclaimed and Latin Grammy Award-winning singer has captivated audiences and fellow artists around the world.

Buika has collaborated with an impressive array of internationally renowned musicians, including Cuban pianist Chucho Valdés, Pat Metheny, Carlos Santana, Anoushka Shankar, and Chick Corea. She also appeared as a singer in Pedro Almodóvar’s film The Skin I Live In (La piel que habito).

When this extraordinary vocalist, songwriter, and poet comes to Stora Teatern, prepare for a journey into a musical universe where a multitude of traditions are brought to life through one singularly expressive voice—truly one of a kind.

Buika – vocals
Santiago Cañada – trombone
Carlos Sarduy – trumpet
Rolando Luna – piano

title: Ultimate Tennis Showdown Gothenburg
content:
UTS, created by coach and entrepreneur Patrick Mouratoglou, will bring eight of the world’s leading male players to the 10,000-seat arena to compete for a prize money pot of USD 1 million.

Stefanos Tsitsipas, Brandon Nakashima, Holger Rune, Alexander Bublik and Luciano Darderi are the first players confirmed for the eight-man field. They will compete at Scandinavium for a prize pool of USD 1 million. The event will also serve as the UTS Tour Super Stage, where the year-end UTS world number one will be crowned.

The competition runs across two days. Day one stages the quarter-finals, with four matches deciding who advances. Day two builds to the climax with classification matches, the semi-finals and the final — five matches in total to crown the champion and settle the year-end standings, with up to USD 511,000 for the ultimate winner of the tournament. Former UTS Champions include Alex de Minaur, Felix Auger-Aliassime, Ben Shelton, Gael Monfils, Casper Ruud and Andrey Rublev.

UTS promises tennis like never before with an innovative, quickfire fan-friendly format designed to engage and encourage eye-catching tennis. Players compete in high intensity, timed matches of 45 minutes each. They are only allowed one serve and can also play UTS bonus cards at pivotal moments during the match.

Crowds are encouraged to cheer between and during the points, creating a high-energy atmosphere more similar to football and handball matches than traditional tennis events. They even hear from the players during the match thanks to live interviews between the quarters.

Tickets go on sale on Wednesday, August 19, at 11:00.
excerpt: The UTS Tour, bringing together unique, fast-paced tennis and electric atmosphere, will make its debut in Sweden in December, at the iconic Scandinavium arena.

Featuring spectacular figure skating, daring aerial performances, and unforgettable moments from Aladdin, Toy Story, and The Little Mermaid, this immersive experience is filled with music, laughter, and magical memories for the whole family.

title: Wings Of AOR 2027
content:
The Wings of AOR Festival has now announced the long-awaited lineup for the 2027 edition. At the same time, regular tickets and the strictly limited VIP tickets have been released for sale for the three-day rock party at Trädgår’n in Gothenburg on April 22–24, 2027. Following the successes in Norrköping, the festival is now growing and moving to Gothenburg. The new venue at Trädgår’n offers larger spaces, an expanded selection of food and drinks, as well as a fantastic, partly weather-protected outdoor area. Being right in the city also provides better international accessibility for visiting audiences.

The organizers A Star Entertainment, Rocknytt, and Skogsröjet have once again succeeded in bringing together some of the biggest and most beloved names in the genre. The result is a line-up that combines international icons with the very best the Swedish melodic rock scene has to offer.

The festival’s three headliners are British legends Magnum, Canadian giants Harem Scarem, and Swedish fan favorites H.E.A.T. They are joined by British AOR veterans FM and acclaimed rising star Chez Kane.

The Swedish contingent is stronger than ever, featuring Gathering of Kings, reunited Dalton, Care of Night, Remedy, Emotional Fire, Vypera, and The Devil Wears Nada. In addition, Transatlantic Radio presents a unique collaboration between top musicians from Sweden and the United States, with the ambition of delivering the very best of melodic rock from both sides of the Atlantic.

Presenter: Stefan Johansson.
excerpt: Three days, three headliners, and a unique lineup of the world’s top AOR and melodic rock acts await as the Wings of AOR Festival takes its next big step in its development.

title: Erna Behind the Camera
content:
The history of the Hasselblad camera company has long been dominated by Victor and his family. But Erna was always by his side. Now, the Hasselblad Foundation presents the exhibition and publication Erna Behind the Camera, which for the first time provides a clearer picture of her decisive importance to the company’s success.

Erna Hasselblad was Victor’s driving force, a board member, and a central figure in the early development of Hasselblad AB. Despite this, her role has often been diminished in historical accounts, due to patriarchal structures, but also because traces of her have been few. The Hasselblad couple lived a public life while remaining deeply private. Upon their passing, personal letters and documents were burned according to their will. By piecing together fragments from newspaper archives, corporate documents, and other archival material, research has now led to new information about Erna’s position and influence.

The exhibition also highlights Erna as a photographer. The Foundation’s collections include the couple’s private photo collection. A closer study reveals that Victor was far from the only one behind the lens. Through images from travels, parties, and social gatherings, we catch glimpses of the world through Erna’s eyes.
excerpt: Erna Hasselblad steps out of the shadows – a new exhibition highlights the woman behind the camera and the company.

title: TATAU – Freedom – Identity – Memory
content:
Tattoos one of humanity’s oldest forms of expression. Throughout history, tattoos have been used to mark identity, life transitions, spirituality, and social belonging. In many cultures, they also function as a living language passed between generations.

In TATAU, we meet women from Tahiti, Canada, Kurdistan, North Africa, the Balkans, the Arctic, Asia, New Zealand, and Sweden. Their tattoos carry stories of family, motherhood, spirituality, resistance, and cultural identity. Many of these tattooing traditions have been threatened or suppressed through colonialism, religious norms, and social change, but are today being revived by new generations.

The exhibition also highlights women’s role in tattoo history – both as carriers of tradition and as active agents in the renewal of cultural expression. Here, tattooing emerges as a tool for memory, healing, and resistance, as well as a way of reconnecting with roots and creating meaning in the present.

TATAU shows that tattoos are more than images on the skin. They are living cultural heritage and personal stories of freedom, identity, and belonging – shaped over time, yet carried in the present.
excerpt: What does a tattoo reveal about the person who wears it? In the exhibition TATAU – Freedom – Identity – Memory, we encounter women’s tattoos from different parts of the world – stories etched into the skin about identity, belonging, and memory.

featuredmedia.alt_text: Kanahus “Freedom” Manuel.

title: Zanele Muholi – Hasselblad Award 2026
content:
Zanele Muholi is an internationally active photographer and visual activist whose work centres on visibility, dignity and the rights of Black LGBTQIA+ communities. Through powerful portraiture and long-term projects such as Faces and Phases and Somnyama Ngonyama, Muholi combines artistic precision with political engagement. The work challenges norms and helps shape alternative visual narratives of identity, representation and resistance.

The exhibition at Hasselblad Center opens on 10 October and will present a selection of Zanele Muholi’s works.

Hasselblad Award 2026

In connection with the award, an extensive programme will take place in Gothenburg, featuring that includes a seminar, an artist talk, a concert with the Gothenburg Symphony Orchestra, a book launch, an exhibition preview, and the formal award ceremony on October 9 . The week highlights the laureate and creates opportunities for dialogue between audiences, artists and researchers within the field of photography.
excerpt: The artist Zanele Muholi has been awarded the 2026Hasselblad Award – the world’s largest photography prize. Their work is presented in an exhibition at the Hasselblad Center 10 October 2026 to 4 of April 2027.

title: Pink Floyd’s – The Dark Side of the Moon
content:
To mark the 50th anniversary of Wish You Were Here, one of Pink Floyd’s most celebrated and influential albums, as well as 50 years of The Dark Side of the Moon, Star Entertainment presents a spectacular concert in Gothenburg.

Wish You Were Here is a deeply emotional concept album, created during a period when the band felt increasingly disconnected from the music industry. It was also written as a tribute to former band member Syd Barrett. Songs such as Shine On You Crazy Diamond, Have a Cigar, Welcome to the Machine and the title track Wish You Were Here have become enduring classics that continue to resonate with audiences around the world.

The Dark Side of the Moon, Pink Floyd’s best-selling album, features iconic tracks including The Great Gig in the Sky, Money, Us and Them and Time.

Experience Pink Floyd’s music performed live by musicians who have toured with Pink Floyd and Roger Waters, and immerse yourself in the timeless soundscapes that helped redefine rock music.

Expect unforgettable melodies, thought-provoking lyrics and a spectacular light and laser show in a concert celebrating two of Pink Floyd’s greatest masterpieces.

title: The World of Sevdah & more
content:
Traditional Balkan sevdah meets rock, classical influences and contemporary world music in this two-hour concert. Dubravko “Duco” Knežević and an ensemble of leading musicians from Sweden and the Balkans present an emotionally charged performance celebrating musical diversity.

The programme features sevdah alongside Greek, Bosnian, Macedonian, Serbian, Romani and Croatian musical traditions, reimagined in powerful new arrangements together with Duco’s own compositions.

The tour visits Sweden, Denmark, Germany, Austria, Switzerland, Slovenia, Croatia, Serbia and Bosnia and Herzegovina, offering audiences a unique opportunity to experience Balkan music from a fresh perspective.

Together, they have also created and produced hundreds of concerts, including Champions of Rock, Sommarkonserter i S:t Anna, Christmas tours and Peter & Bruno, attracting audiences of more than 400,000 people.

Petra Wahlgren grew up in a musical family and works as a freelance singer and violinist. She has performed with many of Sweden’s best-known artists, including Tomas Ledin, Pugh Rogefeldt, Diggiloo, Christmas Night and, most recently, Fröken Elvis. In addition to violin and vocals, she also plays piano and percussion.
excerpt: Peter, Bruno, Matilda and Petra have delighted audiences with their popular Unplugged concert tours for several years. In 2025, the quartet introduced a Christmas edition, combining festive favourites, humour and outstanding musicianship in a concert that became an instant success.

title: Cochemea (US)
content:
Multi-instrumentalist and composer Cochemea Gastelum carries music in his DNA. With more than 25 years on the international stage, he has collaborated with artists including Sharon Jones & The Dap-Kings, Amy Winehouse, The Roots, and Quincy Jones.

Now touring his latest album, Vol. 3: Ancestros Futuros (Daptone Records), Cochemea weaves together past, present, and future into a richly immersive musical experience.

Blending spiritual jazz, funk, and ritualistic soundscapes, Cochemea draws on his Yaqui heritage to explore themes of ancestry, identity, and resilience.

Live, he delivers an intense and hypnotic performance where saxophone, flute, and percussion merge into something both deeply rooted and otherworldly.

title: FaceSoul (UK/Somalia)
content:
London-based artist FaceSoul has quickly emerged as one of the most exciting voices in alternative R&B. Born in Somalia and raised with influences from East African culture and the global diaspora, he creates music where soul, R&B and poetry meet in a deeply personal and stripped-back expression.

With soft harmonies, minimalist production and introspective lyrics, FaceSoul explores themes of identity, faith, healing and human connection. Since his debut EP YSRA, followed by A Beautiful Patience and his acclaimed debut album ARRIVAL (2025), he has built a dedicated international audience and established himself as a unique voice in modern soul.

On November 5, FaceSoul comes to Nefertiti for an intimate evening of soulful melodies and heartfelt storytelling – a concert experience built on presence and connection.

title: Svante Söderqvist – The Rocket
content:
The Rocket brings together two musical worlds in a seamless collaboration: the Swedish Svante Söderqvist Triowith pianist Adam Forkelid and drummer Calle Rasmusson, alongside Swedish-Estonian accordionist and sound explorer Tuulikki Bartosik.

Following the success of their debut album Arrival (2020), the trio began exploring new sonic landscapes, naturally leading to their collaboration with Bartosik. United by a shared love for Swedish folk music and a curiosity for new expressions, the partnership grew into an organic and inspiring musical meeting.

Led by Svante Söderqvist’s melodic and soulful compositions, the project blends jazz, folk influences and experimental textures. His classical-inspired approach allows both double bass and cello to take center stage, sometimes accompanied by wordless vocals.

Bartosik adds a unique layer of sound through her expressive accordion playing, where subtle electronic elements merge seamlessly with the acoustic setting. The result is a constantly evolving musical journey, shaped by the moment.
excerpt: A meeting of acoustic and electronic sounds, where tradition is reimagined through a modern and exploratory lens.

title: Frankly! – A Tribute to Sinatra
content:
Frank Sinatra – A musical icon

With his distinctive baritone voice and impeccable style, Sinatra became a teenage idol during the war years. Over the following decades, his career flourished, and during the 1950s he achieved some of his greatest success as a recording artist with unforgettable hits such as I’ve Got the World on a String andI’ve Got the World on a String I Get a Kick Out of You.

Bohuslän Big Band

Bohuslän Big Band is an orchestra that both preserves and challenges the big band tradition. Over the years, the ensemble has performed with international stars such as Gregory Porter, Maria Schneider and Nils Landgren, as well as beloved Swedish artists including Jill Johnson, Samuel Ljungblahd and Tommy Körberg.

In 2026, the band was also nominated for an American Grammy Award in the category “Best Large Jazz Ensemble Album” for the album Lumen together with Panamanian pianist Danilo Pérez.

They have even been described as “A World Class Jazz Orchestra” by Quincy Jones himself.

Niklas Gabrielsson Lind

Singer, musician and composer Niklas Gabrielsson Lind moves effortlessly between musical genres, with a particular passion for the American jazz vocal tradition and Frank Sinatra as his greatest inspiration.

Niklas has appeared performing his own music in the acclaimed Swedish TV series Vår tid är nu and has also featured in På Spåret. He has performed with ensembles including the Swedish Radio Symphony Orchestra, the Gothenburg Symphony Orchestra, the Royal Stockholm Philharmonic Orchestra and the Ekdahl Bagge Big Band. His jazz project Platina Jazz has also amassed more than 20 million views on YouTube.

Book a Dinner & Concert package and enjoy a carefully crafted two-course dinner at Ceno On Top, where the head chef showcases the flavours of the season.

Duration: approximately 90 minutes, no intermission

title: Händel & Roman with Göteborg Baroque
content:
The connection between Göteborg Baroque and Georg Friedrich Handel is a close one for many reasons, not least because of our unique claviorganum, built after Handel’s own instrument. The bond between Handel and Johan Helmich Roman is equally well known: their paths famously crossed when Roman served as a violinist in Handel’s orchestra at the King’s Theatre in London.

There is something truly special about the meeting between Handel and Roman, and it is this encounter that brings Göteborg Baroque’s season to a close. The programme features highlights from the beloved Drottningholm Music, while our Artistic Director, Magnus Kjellson, takes centre stage as soloist in one of Handel’s organ concertos.

“There is simply nowhere to hide. Everything can be heard. The result is as exposed and personal as it can possibly be. Every solo contribution is clear and heartfelt, and the blend of the ten singers is perfect.”

So wrote Carl Magnus Juliusson in Göteborgs-Posten in 2019, following Göteborg Baroque’s performance of Buxtehude’s Membra Jesu Nostri as part of the ensemble’s 15th anniversary celebrations.

Göteborg Baroque was founded in 2003 by its Artistic Director, Magnus Kjellson, who continues the long-standing tradition of leading the ensemble from the organ or harpsichord while performing. What gives Göteborg Baroque its distinctive sound is the close musical dialogue between its instrumentalists and singers, united by a shared passion for early music.

title: Couperin: Leçons de Ténèbres
content:
Leçons de ténèbres is the name given to the predominantly French tradition of setting the biblical Lamentations to music. Ténèbres means “darkness” and refers both to the literal darkness of the church—where, traditionally, one candle was extinguished after each lesson—and to a symbolic atmosphere of grief, contemplation, and reflection.

The music is based on texts from the Lamentations of Jeremiah and conveys profound emotions of loss, stillness, and hope. It is deeply intimate and expressive, placing the voice at the centre to reveal the emotional depth and subtle beauty of the text.

Intended for performance during Holy Week, the Leçons de ténèbres exist in numerous settings. The most celebrated is François Couperin’s version, composed in 1714 for two voices, viola da gamba, and organ. For many, it is one of the great masterpieces of the Baroque repertoire, whose stripped-back, meditative character speaks directly to the heart.

“There is simply nowhere to hide. Everything can be heard. The result is as exposed and personal as it can possibly be. Every solo contribution is clear and heartfelt, and the blend of the ten singers is perfect.”

So wrote Carl Magnus Juliusson in Göteborgs-Posten in 2019, following Göteborg Baroque’s performance of Buxtehude’s Membra Jesu Nostri as part of the ensemble’s 15th anniversary celebrations.

Göteborg Baroque was founded in 2003 by its Artistic Director, Magnus Kjellson, who continues the long-standing tradition of leading the ensemble from the organ or harpsichord while performing. What gives Göteborg Baroque its distinctive sound is the close musical dialogue between its instrumentalists and singers, united by a shared passion for early music.

title: Evening Song – The Masterpieces by Simone Vesi
content:
It is easy to imagine that the Baroque repertoire has remained untouched for centuries, yet behind every concert programme lies a wealth of scholarly research. Musicologists continue to uncover forgotten treasures, bringing remarkable works to light after centuries beneath the dust of history. One such scholar is the internationally renowned musicologist Kerala Snyder, whose tireless work has been instrumental in reconstructing the music of the composer Simone Vesi.

Recognising Göteborg Baroque’s unique artistry, Snyder selected the ensemble at an early stage to champion Vesi’s music. This collaboration has now culminated in a forthcoming recording devoted to the previously little-known Italian composer. Ahead of the album’s release, we are delighted to present a selection of our favourite works from Vesi’s remarkable oeuvre. Join us for an exclusive preview of this exciting new recording.

title: Mustafa Algiyadi – All New Material
content:
Moving through class, culture and modern life, the Libyan comedian examines the forces quietly shaping our choices. From social pressure to the internet to the dangerous amount of confidence produced by spending too much time inside your own head.

His critically-acclaimed debut show Almost Legal Alien toured across 22 countries and 53 cities and sold out several shows, including a run at the Edinburgh Fringe Festival. Mustafa has opened for Reggie Watts and Todd Barry, earned a spot in The Times’ “Top Jokes of the Edinburgh Fringe 2024,” and drawn coverage in The Guardian, The Scotsman, and The List.

Based in Germany, Mustafa hosts the English night at Munich’s Lucky Punch Comedy Club and is the founder of the longest-running English stand-up comedy night in the city. He trained at The Second City and has a background in improv theatre.

content:

Rogier has toured extensively across Europe, the UK, and Canada since 2024, with many shows selling out and some definitely not! He’s a regular at comedy clubs all over the Netherlands, including the world famous Boom Chicago and Rotterdam-favorite Comedy Club Haug. title: Britta Marakatt–Labba
content:
Over the past decade, Britta Marakatt-Labba has made an almost unparalleled breakthrough. Her embroidered narratives connect the underworld, the upper world and the ground we walk on, in accordance with the worldview of Sámi mythology. With needle and thread, she stitches together the historical and the symbolic, transforming it all into a breathtaking odyssey. Her motifs revolve around Sámi life in close relationship with nature, but also around colonialism, loss and resistance – about the face of racism, human greed and the lost lands once grazed by the animals.

Marakatt-Labba has become internationally renowned for her extraordinary embroideries. Her drawings and watercolours, however, are almost entirely unknown – works she has kept out of the public eye until now. These images, delicate yet powerful, are thematically very close to the embroideries – the same motifs often recur, but in a new and more intimate form.

In the autumn/winter of 2026–2027, The Nordic Watercolour Museum will have the unique opportunity to present the first ever exhibition of Britta Marakatt-Labba’s works on paper. This opens up an entirely new perspective on her artistic practice. The exhibition comprises around 70 works, mainly watercolours and drawings, complemented by a selection of embroideries, sculptures and graphics.

title: Teresia Björk – u&me
content:
In a society where more and more people live alone, while digital technology blurs the line between real and unreal – what do you do with your loneliness?

u&me is a solo about the human capacity for empathy, and how we can experience events and places we have not lived through or visited.

Teresia Björk is one of Sweden’s most established choreographers and dance artists. She has been active as a dancer, actor and choreographer both in Sweden and internationally for the past 35 years, also in close collaborations within the theatre and film world. Her choreography is characterized by sensitivity, precision and a courage to express strong emotions beyond words.

title: Konus Quartet – Lichtkeile
content:
The saxophone quartet is something of a rarity: a new standard ensemble, a sort of modern alternative to the classic string quartet. Compared to its predecessor, it also has several clear advantages: the saxophone has an enormous dynamic range, and by switching between different instruments in the saxophone family, the ensemble can easily shift between registers, from bass to treble.

Switzerland-based Konus Quartet embody this potential for versatility and renewal well, having collaborated closely with many composers and premiered countless works.

This concert centers on a commission by composer Emil Nilsson, who is also a board member of Levande Musik.

title: Jonas Olsson – Lachenmann
content:
Recording the complete piano works of the towering Helmut Lachenmann – what an undertaking! Playing them all in a single concert program? Pianist Jonas Olsson accepts one challenge after the other. This concert traces an oeuvre that stretches over seven decades, mirroring the evolution of our culture from modernity through post-modernity into … whatever we’d like to call our own curious zeitgeist.

His early Schubert variations illustrate Lachenmann’s tendency toward intertextuality, while the classic Guero is a piano piece that is played entirely without pressing any of the keys. The concert comes to a close with Marche fatale, where an 80-year-old Lachenmann explores the banal and ridiculous.

We could easily lose ourselves in fascination with the composer’s unceasing ability to find new ways of producing sound, but Jonas Olsson reminds us that Lachenmann’s music isn’t intended to be about new sounds, but a new way of listening.

A pre-concert talk will be held with Jonas Olsson and Siri Landgren, focusing on Jonas Olsson’s interpretation on Lachenmann’s piano works. Free admission for this talk.
excerpt: Jonas Olsson interprets Helmut Lachenmann in this concert organised by Levande Musik.

title: Work in progress: Lovisa Mattisson & Ami Skånberg
content:
Lovisa Mattisson’s work Drömmar explores the changing course of events and properties of dreams, memories that are processed during the night, and the different stages of sleep. In a solo, with music and sound by Gustav Lejelind, these different states are examined in an atmospheric setting. Moments where dreams sometimes feel more real than reality, and the feeling that can persist after waking up. During the residency, the work focuses on building a feeling and scenography that invites and reinforces the experience of being in the middle of a dream. Sound and music is created by Gustav Lejelind.

In What if?, Ami Skånberg brings together fragments from her performing arts practice since 1987 in preparation for her 40th anniversary as an artist in 2027. Can a Japanese dance fan coexist with punk and Alf Robertson? And does a surfboard have something to say? How might the current political climate and her intensive workshop with Deborah Hay at Vitlycke in September influence the project? During the residency, the work focuses on bringing movement, video, music, objects and memories into unexpected encounters. By experimenting with different performative materials and associations, the project explores how an artistic life can be reflected through fragments, allowing humour, seriousness and curiosity to coexist as new narratives emerge.

Free admission.

title: Lili Re – Studies of a Figure in Green: Chapter 1
content:
Studies of a Figure in Green – Chapter 1 takes aim at humanity’s most passionately confused fantasies about the natural world. Told through a chorus of three voices trapped between ecstatic communion and brutal self-examination, this is a performance about intimacy with nature and the need to belong.

Blending documentary and fiction, the piece draws on the experiments of 1960s CIA agent Cleve Backster, who attached a lie detector to his office plant, claiming to unlock its “inner life”. This curious moment, in between science and mysticism, inspired a performative language that dreams of communication with all living things, while revealing how this desire is haunted by an instinct to dominate.
excerpt: Combining movement, textile, text and video, LiLi Re presents a multi-disciplinary piece that asks: is love for the natural world a deep truth or a dangerous lie?

title: Geiger – Novfest
content:
GEIGER was started around 2004 by a few composers and musicians, several of whom had met at what is now called the Academy of Music and Drama. They started their own to create a place and context for contemporary music, and especially contemporary electronic music. An unpretentious name was chosen: GEIGER (“Gothenburg Electro-acoustic Institute for Grants, Events and Research”). Every syllable in that acronym may not have been realized yet, but there have been a huge number of concerts over the years with music and sound art that otherwise would never have been experienced in Gothenburg.

Since 2006, GEIGER has regularly arranged larger and smaller events at various locations in Gothenburg and this anniversary festival will present a program with both Swedish and international artists.

title: Kassandra Production – The Swamp

The swamp of the internet is impenetrable and sprawling. You get sucked into it, you can’t find what’s up and what’s down, and you can even perish there – and die.
THE SWAMP is a performance about the pitfalls of the internet, and the manipulation and violence that goes on under the radar on the dark web.

In the Swedish premiere of THE SWAMP you are invited into an alluring, mysterious and wildly growing swamp.

title: Israel Aloni/ilDance – A Moment of Endlessness
content:
A Moment of Endlessness emerged from a research process at archaeological sites in Serbia, Spain, Italy, and Greece where choreographer Israel Aloni observed how stories attached to places do more than revive the past: they blur the boundaries between different temporalities, bringing past and present into dialogue.

Texts by Hayim Nahman Bialik and Kohelet (Ecclesiastes) accompany the audience on a journey through moments, images, and sensations that move between the personal and the collective, the intimate and the universal.

A Moment of Endlessness was initially performed within the Dancing Histor(y)ies project, a European collaboration exploring the encounters between contemporary dance and archaeological heritage sites.

With support by Västra Götalandsregionen and Göteborgs stad.
excerpt: A performance that reflects on time as both concept and lived experience, exploring how stories gain meaning through the contexts in which they are told and retold.

title: Katten Konstgrupp – Circle, Circle I + II
content:
In the series, Katten Konstgrupp explores spatial dramaturgy, audience perception, and the dissolution of the boundaries between stage and audience space.

In Part I – Watching a Drama with Others, the story revolves around an unexpected stop on the subway and two friends who meet again after a long time apart. Friendship, grief and transformation are central themes in this concentric part, where three women embody one.

In Part II – The Open Window, symbols and the influence of the unconscious are explored. What dream are you chasing?

Choreographers Fredrika Byman Moberg and Soledad Howe together with composer Malin Dahlström, form Katten Konstgrupp. Drawing on their shared experience in body, dance, music, and audience interaction within the performing arts, they create a dance work/concert in which the audience’s presence and movement become part of the piece. In Circle, Circle, a non-linear narrative unfolds within an immersive space where music is partially performed live.

By and with: Soledad Howe, Malin Dahlström & Fredrika Byman Moberg
Choir: Eden

With support by the city of Gothenburg.
excerpt: Join us for the first and second parts of the triptych Circle, Circle. Choreography and newly composed live music unfold in a world between autofiction and dream.

The pianist Hampus Torarp and the double bassist Jonas Nilsson invite you to a warm, atmospheric and sparkling evening that you will not soon forget.

title: …why do you hold back?
content:
The exhibition unfolds across all floors of the building through a series of site-specific installations. In dialogue with Röda Sten Konsthall’s industrial architecture and its historical connection to the area’s sugar industry, Kastrati explores the relationship between body, machine and labour. Through sculpture, video, sound and monumental reliefs, she draws on materials and narratives connected to confectionery production, examining how repetitive movements and long working hours shape both the body and lived experience.

The exhibition title, …why do you hold back?, is taken from the opening line “My tears, why do you hold back?”, from Barbara Strozzi’s seventeenth-century composition Lagrime mie. The question echoes throughout the exhibition, giving form to the tension between silence and expression, restraint and resistance.

Doruntina Kastrati represented Kosovo at the 2024 Venice Biennale, where she received a Special Mention for The Echoing Silences of Metal and Skin. Most of the works in the exhibition have been created specifically for Röda Sten Konsthall.

Curated by Amila Puzić.

Opening September 12

title: The Grissini Project The music of Hans Zimmer vs John Williams
content:
On the set list are unforgettable themes from legendary films and sagas such as Star Wars, Harry Potter, Jurassic Park, Indiana Jones, Pirates of the Caribbean, The Dark Knight, Interstellar, Gladiator, Inception and many more.

title: Exhibition opening: Ilona Sagar: Omsorgens arkitektur
content:
How does architecture shape our health and well-being? Building on Ilona Sagar’s immersive film installation Other Actors (2025), the exhibition explores the links between bodies, health, and architecture through the lens of Aino and Alvar Aalto’s tuberculosis sanatorium in Paimio, Finland. Together with some twenty design objects and archival material from the sanatorium, the exhibition offers a deeper insight into one of the Nordic region’s most acclaimed modernist buildings. The exhibition takes its title, Omsorgens arkitektur, from the Swedish word omsorg, referring to an attentive and holistic approach to care.

The opening begins at 13:00 with welcome remarks by artist Ilona Sagar, Museum Director Nina Due and curator Olivia Berkowicz. Refreshments and mingling will follow.

At 14:00-14.30, Ilona Sagar and Olivia Berkowicz will lead an exclusive guided tour. The artist Flis Holland will introduce their collaboration with Sagar on the Paimio chair audio piece in the exhibition.

Read more about Ilona Sagar: Omsorgens arkitektur.

title: Ilona Sagar: Omsorgens arkitektur
content:
Step into the sanatorium’s colour palette and experience its iconic colour combinations. On the custom-built, reclining sofa, you can sit back and experience Aino Marsio-Aalto and Alvar Aalto’s idea of the horizontal body.

Through accounts from doctors, nurses, and maintenance staff, multiple perspectives on Paimio Sanatorium emerge in Ilona Sagar’s work Other Actors. Together with some twenty design objects and archival material from the sanatorium, the exhibition offers a deeper insight into one of the Nordic region’s most acclaimed modernist buildings.

A groundbreaking idea in the design of the sanatorium was to adapt its rooms for patients who spent long periods in bed. The Aaltos conceived the building as a “medical instrument”, designed around the needs of the reclining body rather than the standing one. Here, a more humane and softer form of modernism emerges, in which light, ventilation, and heating were shaped with the body in its most vulnerable state in mind. The sanatorium also became known for its distinctive palette of green, blue, red, orange, and yellow.

“Omsorg is a Swedish word for care, but also concern, expressing a form of attentive, holistic care historically embedded in civic structures that shapes both people and the spaces they inhabit. This ethic of care lies at the heart of the exhibition Ilona Sagar: Omsorgens arkitektur.” – Ilona Sagar.

Ilona Sagar

Moving image, text, performance, and installation are central to the practice of London-based artist and filmmaker Ilona Sagar. Drawing on archival research and interdisciplinary collaboration, her work explores how civic and social identities are constructed and contested through the infrastructures of health, technology and the body. Sagar approaches historical archives and institutions, not as an encounter with a safely sealed past, but as something current and unstable that speaks urgently to our present condition.

Aino Marsio-Aalto and Alvar Aalto

Aino Marsio-Aalto (1894–1949) and Alvar Aalto (1898–1976) are among Finland’s most influential figures in modern architecture and design. Together, they developed an approach in which architecture, furniture, and everyday objects were conceived in relation to one another. During the 1920s and 1930s, they designed several pioneering buildings centred on human needs. Their international breakthrough came with the tuberculosis sanatorium in Paimio, Finland, completed in 1933. This year marks the 50th anniversary of Alvar Aalto’s death.

The exhibition is supported by Kulturfonden för Sverige och Finland.

The exhibition is designed by Adrien Rovero.

Top image: Ilona Sagar, Other Actors, 2025.
excerpt: Building on Ilona Sagar’s film installation “Other Actors” (2025), the exhibition explores the links between bodies, health, and architecture through the lens of Aino Marsio-Aalto and Alvar Aalto’s tuberculosis sanatorium in Paimio, Finland.

title: Yokai – Spirits of Japan
content:
Yokai are Japanese spirits or creatures—beloved, feared, and an integral part of popular culture for hundreds of years.

Stories about yokai have been told for over a thousand years. In this first major Swedish exhibition on yokai, you first meet them in the masterful scroll paintings, woodcuts and netsukes of the Edo period (1603–1868) and then follow their evolution into today’s computer games, horror films and anime.

There are several types of yokai. Among the most popular are Tanuki, a cunning and playful raccoon dog. Another example is ghosts or spirits – Yurei. These are so terrifying that there is a tradition of telling stories about them on warm summer evenings so that the chills cool down the listener!
excerpt: Humans have always sought explanations for strange phenomena, unusual dreams, or the feeling of an invisible presence. In Japanese folklore, such occurrences are often explained through yokai.

The rabbits love a celebration and simply can’t wait! That’s why they’re opening the gates to Kaninlandet as early as September 26, for an extra-fluffy preview of the autumn fun. Expect thrilling rides, a bouncy disco, rabbit theatre, mischief, play and, of course, plenty of sweets. Spooktacular fun for the whole family!

On these dates, only Kaninlandet is open. The rest of Liseberg amusement park opens for Halloween on October 2.

title: James Blunt
content:
Since breaking through with “You’re Beautiful” and the debut album Back to Bedlam, James Blunt has established himself as one of the most celebrated songwriters and live performers of the 21st century. His catalogue includes both powerful, emotionally charged ballads such as “Goodbye My Lover”, “High” and “Monsters”, as well as uplifting pop hits like “1973”, “Bonfire Heart” and “Stay the Night”.

His new album Airplane Mode brings together twelve songs that move between melodic pop and emotional depth, all delivered with James Blunt’s signature ability to balance the grand and the intimate.
excerpt: James Blunt is coming to Gothenburg for the very first time. On 17 March, the British singer-songwriter will take the stage at Scandinavium for a concert featuring songs from throughout his career, including material from his new album Airplane Mode.

title: Stjärnorna gnistra & glimma på Draken Live
content:
A sparkling Christmas concert featuring two of the Nordic region’s most acclaimed musical theatre voices – Viktoria Tocca and Fred Johanson.

This atmospheric concert brings together Swedish Christmas traditions and the glamour of international musical theatre in an elegant musical experience. Beloved Swedish classics such as O Helga natt and Stilla natt are interspersed with American Christmas favourites including Winter Wonderland and The Christmas Song, alongside carefully selected gems from the international musical theatre repertoire.

The evening also features a reading from Viktor Rydberg’s classic poem Tomten, creating a warm and festive Christmas atmosphere where tradition meets musical brilliance.

With their powerful voices and long careers on some of the world’s leading musical theatre stages, Viktoria Tocca and Fred Johanson offer a concert filled with elegance, presence and outstanding musical performances.
excerpt: A Christmas concert with Viktoria Tocca and Fred Johanson.

featuredmedia.alt_text: Poster featuring Viktoria Tocca and Fred Johanson against a blue background with stars.

title: The Fantastic Four 2026
content:
Tuxedos, microphone stands, dance moves, singalong numbers and soaring ballads – The Fantastic Four offer a joyful mix of it all for Christmas 2026.

Expect the best of the best! And, of course, O helga natt, White Christmas and other Christmas classics – all performed in the band’s unique old-fashioned style.

This year, The Sugar Peaks are joining the tour. The two-piece brass section don’t just take to the stage – they raise the roof. With blazing trumpets and an irresistible groove, they bring even more soul, even more Motown and even more energy to the show.

There are hints of Old Hollywood, and perhaps even a touch of Frank Sinatra. But with an added sense of fun. And none of it feels contrived – The Fantastic Four have been playing together for almost twenty-five years and still have a fantastic time every time they take to the stage.

For younger audiences, this may be something completely new; for older audiences, it will be a nostalgic trip down memory lane. Stock up on candy canes and polish those dancing shoes.

Presented by Kulturaktiebolaget.
